value_source: AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background
variable_description: Whether a teacher who has taught the child for less than a month said they could still assess the child accurately. The AEDC Data Dictionary describes the variable as establishing "if the teacher is confident in their knowledge of this child to report accurately for the AEDC", and the question is only put where TMSCH records that the child has been in the class less than one month. It is asked only where TMSCH records that the child has been in the class for less than one month, and a teacher who answers No may leave the rest of the instrument blank. In PLIDA it sits on the core table from the 2012 cycle onward, so there is no 2012-style flag for 2009.
value_definition: One integer: 0 for No and 1 for Yes. It is empty for the great majority of children, because the question is only asked where TMSCH shows the child has been in the class for less than a month.
limitation: A Yes is the teacher's own judgement about how well they know the child, not a check on what they then reported, so it flags nothing about answer quality among the teachers who have known a child longer. A No does not remove the child from the file, but it usually leaves the instrument items unanswered, which is what then makes a domain score unavailable.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary gives the variable's purpose, its instrument wording, its filter on TMSCH and its two field values, and the AEDC Data Guidelines state the validity rule that makes the answer matter.
evidence_quote: This variable establishes if the teacher is confident in their knowledge of this child to report accurately for the AEDC.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Can assess child', gave 'finite source-defined values' as the domain and the generic 'The valid_values field contains the source-defined values.' sentence as the value definition, so nothing explained that the question is asked only of teachers new to the child, or that it governs whether the child's domain scores count.

value_domain: AEDC yes/no home language communication flag
value_source: AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the teacher thinks the child can communicate adequately in the home language named on the same row, which is a language other than English. The AEDC Data Dictionary gives the instrument wording as "Can this child adequately communicate in this language (languageID or ilanguageID)?", so the language in question is the one in LANGUAGEID beside it, not English. It is only asked where LANG in the core table records that the child speaks a language other than English at home. The LANGSOURCE0 to LANGSOURCE4 flags on the same row say what the teacher based the answer on: an enrolment form or report, a parent or relative, their own observation, another staff member, or another source.
value_definition: One integer: 0 for No, 1 for Yes and 88 for Don't know, the AEDC's standard code for a question the teacher cannot answer.
limitation: It says nothing about the child's English, which the instrument records in a separate proficiency item, so a Yes here is no evidence that the child can follow classroom English. It is also a teacher's judgement about a language they may not speak, which is why the LANGSOURCE flags record where the answer came from.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary gives this variable's purpose, its instrument wording naming LanguageID and iLanguageID, its filter on the Lang item and its three field values, and the PLIDA language table carries LANGUAGEID and the LANGSOURCE flags on the same row.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child can communicate adequately in this language (languageID or ilanguageID).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Can adequately communicate in this language' with no statement of which language that is, and printed the generic 'The valid_values field contains the source-defined values.' sentence as its value definition, so a reader could easily have taken it for a measure of English.

value_source: AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background
variable_description: Whether the class the child was assessed in mixes several school year levels. The AEDC Data Dictionary defines a multi-year class as "one that includes students of various ages, abilities and school year levels". Where the answer is Yes, CLASSTYPEA_2 on the same row records which year levels are combined. It describes the class rather than the child, so every child that teacher assessed in that class carries the same answer.
value_definition: One integer: 0 for No and 1 for Yes.
limitation: It describes the make-up of the class, not the child's own year level, so it cannot tell you whether the child was among the youngest or the oldest in the room. It also says nothing about class size or how the teacher grouped children within it.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the data element, gives its instrument wording and its two field values, and records that CLASSTYPEA_2 is only asked when this item is Yes.
evidence_quote: A multi-year class is one that includes students of various ages, abilities and school year levels.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Multi-year class' with 'finite source-defined values' as its domain and the generic value-definition sentence, so it never said what a multi-year class is or that the flag describes the class rather than the child.

value_source: AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background
variable_description: Which year levels the child's multi-year class combines, asked only where CLASSTYPEA_1 records that it is a multi-year class. The AEDC Data Dictionary explains that "A first year class may combine preparatory and/or year 1 and/or year 2 levels, or include an alternate combination of other students", and the three codes follow that shape: preparatory with year 1, preparatory with years 1 and 2, or another combination. Like the flag it depends on, it is an attribute of the class, so it repeats across every child that teacher assessed.
value_definition: One integer: 1 for Preparatory and Grade/Year 1, 2 for Preparatory, Grade/Year 1 and Grade/Year 2, and 3 for Other. It is empty wherever CLASSTYPEA_1 is No.
limitation: The Other code absorbs every combination outside the two named ones and cannot be broken down further. The states and territories also name the first year of school differently, and the code does not record which name applies, nor how many children sit in each year level.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the data element, states the filter 'Only if ClassTypeA_1 = Yes', and lists the three field values in full.
evidence_quote: A first year class may combine preparatory and/or year 1 and/or year 2 levels, or include an alternate combination of other students.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Type of multi-year class' and gave the generic 'The valid_values field contains the source-defined values.' sentence, so the three codes were unlabelled and the dependence on CLASSTYPEA_1 went unstated.

value_source: AEDC 2025 Data Dictionary, section 9 Instrument Background
variable_description: Whether the child was repeating the year level they were in when the teacher completed the instrument. The AEDC Data Dictionary explains that a school may recommend a child "remain in the same year level, or grade, for another year in order to improve their skills, knowledge and/or wellbeing before moving onto the next school level". Because the AEDC is collected in a child's first year of full-time school, a Yes marks a child doing that first year a second time, which usually also means they are older than their classmates.
value_definition: One integer: 0 for No and 1 for Yes.
limitation: It does not say why the child is repeating, who decided, or whether the earlier year was at the same school. Age is held separately in AGEINMONTHS and the age category columns, so the flag should be read beside those rather than used as a proxy for being older than the class.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary defines the data element, gives its purpose as identifying whether the child is repeating the year or grade, and lists its two field values.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child is repeating this year/grade.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Child repeating this grade', with 'finite source-defined values' as its domain and the generic value-definition sentence, so it never explained what repeating means in a first-year-of-school collection or how it relates to the age columns.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ClassTypeC
variable_description: Whether the child was enrolled in more than one educational setting when the teacher completed the instrument. The AEDC defines dual placement as "when the child is co-enrolled at two or more educational institutions, or in two or more educational programs", and the teacher answers it for every child in the class. From the 2018 cycle CLASSTYPEC_2 sits beside it and names which kind of second placement it was, asked only where this column is 1. It matters for reading the rest of the row, because the responding teacher sees a dual-placed child for only part of their school life.
value_definition: A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes. It comes from the AvEDI rather than from a derivation, and it runs in all six collection cycles from 2009.
limitation: It does not say how much of the week the second placement takes, or which of the two settings the responding teacher works in. A child splitting the week evenly between a mainstream class and a special education programme and a child attending a language school for one hour carry the same 1.
rationale: The Data Dictionary gives ClassTypeC its own page with the definition of dual placement, the instrument wording, the 0/1 field values and the cycle it was introduced.
evidence_quote: Dual placement is when the child is co-enrolled at two or more educational institutions, or in two or more educational programs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Dual placement', with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what dual placement means or that a second column names its type.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ClassTypeC_2
variable_description: Which kind of second setting a dual-placed child attends: a special education program, a language school, or something else. The dictionary instructs that it is asked "Only if ClassTypeC = Yes", so a missing value here is the filter working rather than a teacher declining to answer. It appears in the PLIDA 2018, 2021 and 2024 core tables only, so the type of dual placement cannot be recovered for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles even though CLASSTYPEC itself runs across all six.
value_definition: A one-digit integer with three categories: 1 special education program, 2 language school, 3 other.
limitation: It records one type only, so a child co-enrolled in both a special education programme and a language school cannot be represented, and code 3 carries no free text saying what the other setting was.
rationale: The Data Dictionary publishes the three field values, the conditional filter on ClassTypeC and the instrument wording for this element.
evidence_quote: Only if ClassTypeC = Yes
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Type of dual placement', and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the column is conditional on CLASSTYPEC or that only three settings are distinguished.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 and data element COMGEN
variable_description: The child's score on communication skills and general knowledge, one of the five AEDC developmental domains. It is derived from the teacher's answers to the domain's instrument items rather than reported directly, and the AEDC calculates it only "provided that each child has 75 per cent or more of these items completed". Three columns beside it do the interpreting: COMGENVALID says whether the score may be used, COMGENCATEGORY places it in the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands, and COMGEN_1 is the single sub-domain sitting underneath it.
value_definition: A numeric field carried to four decimal places, on a scale where "children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development". There is no code list; the domain is the continuous range.
limitation: It is not an individual diagnosis. The AEDC states that its indicators "have been developed and validated for use as a population measure at a group level and have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children", so a low score for one child carries far less meaning than a low share across a community. The scoring method is licensed from McMaster University and is not published, so the number cannot be recomputed or audited from the item responses held in the same file.
rationale: Section 3.1 of the Data Dictionary sets out the domain scoring rule, the zero-to-ten scale and the 75 per cent completion threshold, and the COMGEN element page gives the 7.4 numeric field format and the derived source.
evidence_quote: For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Communication and general knowledge', and the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, which left the reader with no scale, no direction and no idea that the score is a group-level measure.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 and data element COMGENCategory
variable_description: Where the child's communication and general knowledge score falls in the national score distribution, banded into four percentile groups. Code 1 is the 0 to 10th percentile, which is what the AEDC reports as developmentally vulnerable on this domain, and it is the column most published AEDC vulnerability figures for communication are built from. The cut-offs are fixed at the 2009 baseline: the dictionary records that "the cut-off scores used in 2009 have remained the same across each collection cycle", so a rise in the share coded 1 is a real fall in scores rather than a moving benchmark.
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four bands: 1 = 0 to 10th percentile, 2 = 11th to 25th, 3 = 26th to 50th, 4 = 51st to 100th. The percentiles are those of the 2009 national distribution, not of the child's own cycle.
limitation: It is not calculated for every child. The dictionary states that "Domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs, or children less than four years of age", so a missing value here is usually an exclusion rule rather than an unanswered question, and treating missing as low would count excluded children as scoring well.
rationale: The COMGENCategory element page publishes the four percentile bands verbatim, and section 3.1 states the 2009 baseline rule and the exclusions applied to the domain categories.
evidence_quote: Domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs, or children less than four years of age.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Vulnerable - communication' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the four bands nor said that vulnerability means the bottom decile of a fixed 2009 distribution.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element COMGENValid
variable_description: Whether the child's communication and general knowledge score may be used, and the gate the AEDC applies before reporting COMGEN or COMGENCATEGORY. The dictionary sets 0 to mean the "Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain" and 1 to mean the child meets all three conditions, so a score can exist in the file and still be flagged out of scope. PHYSVALID, SOCVALID, EMOTVALID and LANGCOGVALID apply the identical test to the other four domains, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five a child has a valid score for.
value_definition: A one-digit integer: 0 not valid for reporting, 1 valid. The two labels are the same wording used on every AEDC domain validity flag.
limitation: It does not say which of the three reasons applies. Anyone who wants to keep children with special needs but drop those with too few completed items has to rebuild the test from SPECIALNEEDS, the age columns and the instrument item responses, because this single code cannot separate an excluded three-year-old from a child whose teacher left half the domain blank.
rationale: The COMGENValid element page publishes both field values with their full labels, and the same labels recur on the four sibling domain validity flags, confirming the pattern.
evidence_quote: Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Valid - communication and general knowledge' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding the fact that the flag collapses three different exclusions into one code.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element CommunityID and section 4.1
variable_description: The AEDC community the child was assigned to, held as a six-digit code, with COMMUNITY carrying the matching name. The dictionary defines it as "A unique code to indicate each AEDC community". AEDC communities are a purpose-built reporting geography, not an ABS classification: they are drawn so that "the AEDC boundaries are brought into alignment with the SA1 (Statistical Area 1) building blocks in most cases", while LGACODE, SA2CODE and SA3CODE on the same row carry the ABS geographies. LOCALCOMMUNITYID is the finer level below it.
value_definition: A six-digit integer. The code list is too large for the dictionary and is published separately in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, so the domain is closed but not printed with the element.
limitation: The same code and name do not always cover the same ground across cycles. The AEDC redrew community boundaries for the 2024 collection and applied them back to all six collections, which means figures computed from this column can differ from the numbers the AEDC published at the time. The code also says nothing about whether a community's results may be released, which is what CPUBLIC carries.
rationale: The CommunityID element page gives the definition, the six-digit integer format and the pointer to the reference tables, and section 4.1 explains how AEDC communities relate to ABS geography and how the 2024 boundary revision was backcast.
evidence_quote: A unique code to indicate each AEDC community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Community identifier' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which said nothing about the geography being AEDC-specific or about the retrospective boundary change.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element Consult
variable_description: Whether an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant helped the teacher complete the instrument for this child. The AEDC states its purpose as "To identify if the teacher completing the AvEDI is being assisted by discussion with an Indigenous Consultant", and the item is asked "Only answer if ATSI = Yes", so the column is confined to children identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and a blank on a non-Indigenous child is the filter, not a refusal. Where it is 1, CONSULTTYPE1 to CONSULTTYPE13 record the consultant's job title in the 2009 to 2015 tables and, from the 2012 cycle, CONSULTROLE records what the consultant actually did.
value_definition: A one-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes.
limitation: It records that a consultant was involved, not that the involvement changed anything. It is also not a measure of the teacher's cultural competence: a 0 covers a teacher who is themselves Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, which TEACHERATSI on the same row records, as readily as a teacher with no Indigenous input at all.
rationale: The Consult element page gives the purpose, the instrument wording, the conditional filter on ATSI and the 0/1 field values, and the dictionary's variable index uses the same short label the PLIDA metadata carries.
evidence_quote: Is your completion of the AvEDI being assisted by discussion with an Indigenous Consultant
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Assisted by ATSICC' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving the acronym unexpanded and the ATSI filter unstated, so a reader could not tell that missing values are structural.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element ConsultRole
variable_description: What the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Consultant did for this child, coded four ways from joint completion of the instrument down to general advice unrelated to the child. The dictionary describes the consultant as able to assist "by providing information regarding the child; in regards to the AEDC survey; or in a general advisory capacity", and the item is asked "Only answer if Consult = Yes". It runs in the PLIDA 2012 to 2024 Indigenous tables and not in 2009, so the depth of consultation cannot be assessed for the first cycle even where CONSULT is 1.
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four categories: 1 the consultant and teacher completed the instrument together, 2 the consultant gave general advice about the child, 3 the consultant gave general advice about completing the instrument but not about this child, 4 other.
limitation: Only codes 1 and 2 involve the child at all. Treating any non-missing value as consultation about this child overstates it, because code 3 explicitly covers advice that was not child-specific. The column is also a different question from the consultant's job title, which sits in the separate CONSULTTYPE1 to CONSULTTYPE13 flags and which PLIDA carries for the 2009 to 2015 cycles only.
rationale: The ConsultRole element page publishes all four field values with their full labels, the description of the consultant's possible roles, and the conditional filter on Consult.
evidence_quote: ICC has provided general advice about completing the AvEDI but not specific to this child
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'ATSICC role' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never distinguished a consultant who helped answer for this child from one who gave the teacher general advice.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element CreationDate
variable_description: The day the AEDC extract file was built, not a date about the child. It takes the same value on every row of a cycle's file, so its only real use is telling which vintage of the AEDC data a PLIDA table was cut from. The dictionary lists it as a derived field carried on the complete, core and linkage AEDC files and introduced in the 2012 cycle, although PLIDA carries the column in all six core tables, 2009 included.
value_definition: A ten-character text field holding a date. It is typed as text rather than as a date, so it sorts alphabetically unless it is parsed first.
limitation: It cannot date anything the child did. The collection year is YEAR and the month the teacher completed the instrument is MOC; using this column to order children or to work out age at assessment would substitute the file's build date for the child's own timing.
rationale: The CreationDate element page gives the derived source, the file-creation purpose, the ten-character text format and the 2012 introduction, which together fix it as extract metadata rather than child-level content.
evidence_quote: File creation date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'File creation date' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the value is constant within a file and is not usable as an event date.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element Cycle, table 1 and section 2.3
variable_description: Which of the six triennial AEDC collections the row belongs to, numbered 1 to 6 for 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024. The dictionary defines it simply as "The AEDC collection cycle". It is not interchangeable with YEAR: cycle 1 spans both 2009 and 2010, and the AEDC directs that "2010 data is excluded from all results except Community / Local Community level results". Grouping on this column is how a PLIDA user reproduces an AEDC published figure, since every AEDC report is organised by cycle.
value_definition: A one-digit integer from 1 to 6, one value per collection: 1 = 2009, 2 = 2012, 3 = 2015, 4 = 2018, 5 = 2021, 6 = 2024.
limitation: It does not make cycles comparable. Several instrument items changed between collections, most visibly the condition items D1 to D9 which gained a separate 'yes but does not affect learning' code from cycle 3, and community boundaries were redrawn for cycle 6 and applied backwards, so a trend built by grouping on this column alone can be comparing different questions or different areas.
rationale: The Cycle element page gives the definition and the one-digit format, table 1 maps each cycle number to its collection year, and section 2.3 states the 2009/2010 overlap and the exclusion rule.
evidence_quote: For the 2009 data collection, the Year differs from Cycle variable as the later includes both 2009 and 2010 years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'AEDC cycle' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without the cycle-to-year mapping, which is the one thing a reader needs to join AEDC output to a published report.

value_domain: AEDC condition item with learning-effect codes
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D1
variable_description: Whether the child has a physical disability and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning. The AEDC's purpose for the item is "To identify if the child has a physical disability that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom", and it is the first of nine condition items D1 to D9 the teacher answers for every child. The code frame carries its own history: code 3 is a plain yes used only in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, while codes 1 and 2 split that yes into affects learning and does not affect learning from 2015 onwards.
value_definition: A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes and affects learning (cycle 3 onwards), 2 yes but does not affect learning (cycle 3 onwards), 3 yes (cycles 1 and 2), 88 don't know.
limitation: Counting only code 1 produces a false break at 2015, because the same children were coded 3 in the two earlier cycles; any yes count has to add 1, 2 and 3. The column also names no condition and no severity, and the judgement that learning is affected is the classroom teacher's, not a clinical assessment.
rationale: The D1 element page publishes all five field values with their cycle qualifiers, the instrument wording, and the 2015 revision note recording that code 2 was added.
evidence_quote: Field values and instrument text revised: Added code 2 "Yes - but does not affect learning".
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Physical disability' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which hid the mid-series code frame change that breaks any naive trend.

value_domain: AEDC condition item with learning-effect codes
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D2
variable_description: Whether the child has a visual impairment and, from the 2015 cycle, whether it affects their learning. The AEDC's purpose is "To identify if the child has a visual impairment that affects their ability to do school work in a regular classroom". It sits with D1 physical disability and D3 hearing impairment as the sensory and physical items answered for every child, and from the 2015 tables DIAGNOSIS7 separately records blindness where that is the diagnosis qualifying the child as special needs.
value_definition: A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes and affects learning (cycle 3 onwards), 2 yes but does not affect learning (cycle 3 onwards), 3 yes (cycles 1 and 2), 88 don't know.
limitation: It cannot find undetected vision problems. Many children have their first eye test after starting school, so a child who cannot see the board but has never been assessed reads as 0, and the column also does not say whether an impairment is corrected by glasses already in use.
rationale: The D2 element page publishes the five field values with their cycle qualifiers, the instrument wording and the 2015 revision that added the does-not-affect-learning code.
evidence_quote: Variable to indicate if the child has a visual impairment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Visual impairment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither gave the code frame nor warned that yes was recorded differently before 2015.

value_domain: AEDC other specific condition gate item
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 7.0, February 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, data element D10
variable_description: The gate question for the child's other conditions: whether the child has any specific condition apart from a diagnosis that already qualifies them as special needs. The AEDC's purpose is "To identify if the child has some other specific condition", and beneath it sit the named flags D10AY through D10ZY, one per condition. It entered the instrument in the 2015 cycle and appears in the PLIDA 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024 special-needs tables.
value_definition: A two-digit integer: 0 no, 1 yes, 88 don't know, the AvEDI's standard code for an item the teacher could not answer.
limitation: It says nothing about how many conditions or which ones, and the named condition flags below it only reach PLIDA from the 2018 table, so for the 2015 cycle a 1 here cannot be resolved into anything. A 0 also does not rule out a qualifying diagnosis, which is what SPECIALNEEDS and the DIAGNOSIS series record.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item D3
variable_description: Whether the child's teacher reported a hearing impairment, one of the nine emerging-needs items D1 to D9 recorded for every child on the teacher instrument. value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 0 no, 1 "Yes - affects learning (Cycle 3 onwards)", 2 "Yes - does not affect learning (Cycle 3 onwards)", 3 "Yes (Cycle 1 and 2)" and 88 don't know. value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DevDiff and Appendix 3 section A2.2.1
variable_description: A derived summary flag set when the teacher reported at least one condition, impairment or problem that affects the child's learning. The dictionary publishes the syntax as "IF (D1 EQ 1 OR D2 EQ 1 OR D3 EQ 1 OR D4 EQ 1 OR D5 EQ 1 OR D6 EQ 1 OR D7 EQ 1 OR D8 EQ 1 OR D9 EQ 1 OR D10a EQ 1 OR D10b EQ 1 OR D10c EQ 1) DevDiff=1", so it is built entirely from the D columns sitting beside it in this table rather than from a question of its own. value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1 and section 3.2 Summary Indicators
variable_description: Whether the child was developmentally vulnerable on one or more of the five AEDC domains, the headline AEDC result. The dictionary describes it as "Vulnerable - One or more domains" and notes that "Vulnerability Summary Indicators do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on", so it is derived from PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY beside it. rationale: The dictionary defines the element, explains in section 3.2 how the summary indicators are built from the domain categories, and states the exclusions that make the raw column unsafe to average.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary 2025, item DV1Flag and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
variable_description: Whether the child belongs in the denominator when a developmentally-vulnerable-on-one-or-more rate is calculated. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of DV1" and explains that the flag exists because, when the Canadian Early Development Instrument was adapted for Australia, "work was conducted to refine the denominator (i.e., valid cases) for these two indicators to maximise the number of cases with reportable data". evidence_quote: Two new variables, DV1Flag and DV2Flag, were created in the dataset to define this information.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.2 Summary Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child fell in the lowest AEDC category on at least two of the five developmental domains, the headline measure the AEDC reports as developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains. It is built by counting how many of PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY equal 1, the 0 to 10th percentile band of the 2009 national baseline. The dictionary notes that summary indicators "do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on". DV2FLAG on the same row says whether the child counts in the denominator when the percentage is worked out.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. It is derived rather than collected, and the dictionary publishes no separate code for children who fall outside the DV2 denominator.
limitation: It is not a count of vulnerable domains, so it cannot separate a child vulnerable on two domains from one vulnerable on all five; LOWTOTAL carries the count. A 0 also does not prove the child was assessed on all five domains, because children excluded from the denominator can read as 0, which is exactly why DV2FLAG exists.
rationale: The dictionary defines DV2 as the developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains summary indicator, and section 3.2 explains that the indicator is calculated from the count of vulnerable domains rather than from a score of its own.
evidence_quote: Vulnerability Summary Indicators do not have a score or cut-off scores as they are calculated from the number of domains a child is vulnerable on.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's phrase 'Vulnerable - two or more domains' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said which domains were counted, against what cut-off, or that a companion denominator flag exists.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether this child belongs in the denominator when the percentage developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains is calculated. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains", which means a correct DV2 rate is the mean of DV2 over the rows where this flag is 1, not over all rows. It exists because children with a special needs diagnosis, children aged three and children with too few valid domain scores are excluded from AEDC vulnerability reporting.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes. Derived from the per-domain validity flags together with special needs status and age.
limitation: It says nothing about the child's development, so filtering on it selects a reporting population rather than a vulnerable one. It is also not interchangeable with the per-domain validity flags such as EMOTVALID: a child can hold a valid score on one domain and still fail to qualify for the DV2 denominator.
rationale: The dictionary publishes DV2Flag as a derived denominator qualification variable with a 0/1 value list, alongside the per-domain validity flags that describe the exclusions it is built from.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally vulnerable on two or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording 'Qualifies for the denominator of dv2' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader had no way to know that AEDC vulnerability rates must be computed over this flag rather than over every row.

value_domain: AEDC teacher-reported early intervention attendance (yes/no/don't know)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E1
variable_description: The teacher's report of whether the child had attended an early intervention program before starting school, asked as "To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program". In the special needs table it sits with D1 to D10, the enduring problem flags for physical, sensory, speech, learning, emotional and behavioural difficulties, and with D11 which asks whether the child needs further assessment, so it is the service-use column beside a set of need columns. It is the closest thing the AEDC holds to a record of a child having received support before school entry.
value_definition: A two-digit integer: 0 for no, 1 for yes and 88 for the standard AEDC don't-know code.
limitation: It names no program, no provider, no age at entry and no duration, so it cannot distinguish a single speech pathology block from three years of intensive support. Because the answer is the teacher's, 88 records only that the teacher did not know, and a 0 can mean the teacher was unaware rather than that no program was attended.
rationale: The dictionary gives E1 as an instrument item with its exact question wording and a three-value code list, and the registry places it in the AEDC special needs table beside the D-series problem indicators.
evidence_quote: To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended an early intervention program
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Attended an early intervention program' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not record that the answer is a teacher's report or that 88 codes don't know.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2ay
variable_description: How many hours a week, on average, the child attended the preschool or kindergarten program reported in E2Y, banded around the fifteen-hour national benchmark. The dictionary states its purpose as "To identify if the child was in regular educational programs for the mandatory amount of time", so the three bands are less than fifteen hours, fifteen hours, and more than fifteen hours. It is only answered where E2Y records attendance, and E2BY on the same row says what kind of setting the program ran in.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for less than 15 hours per week, 2 for 15 hours per week, 3 for more than 15 hours per week, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.
limitation: It records a weekly average, not how long the child stayed enrolled, so a child who attended fifteen hours a week for one term is indistinguishable from one who did so for the full year. The bands also carry no information about attendance actually taken up, only about the program the child was enrolled in.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the item wording, its 2018 introduction and the four-code band list, and the registry places it alongside E2Y and E2BY in the same core table.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child was in regular educational programs for the mandatory amount of time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the raw question stem 'To the best of your knowledge did the child attend the preschool / kindergarten program on average:' with no completion, and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the answer categories were entirely missing.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2by
variable_description: What kind of service delivered the preschool or kindergarten program the child attended in the year before school, separating a standalone preschool or kindergarten from a long day care centre. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "the organisational basis for the child's preschool / kindergarten", which is the distinction most Australian early childhood policy work needs, because the same entitlement is delivered through both service types. It is answered only where E2Y records attendance, and E2AY gives the hours.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for preschool or kindergarten, 2 for long day care centre, 3 for other, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in the 2018 cycle.
limitation: It identifies a setting type, not a provider, a funding source or a governance arrangement, so it cannot separate a government preschool from an independent or community one. Code 3 is an undifferentiated catch-all, so mobile, occasional care and school-attached services cannot be told apart from one another.
rationale: The dictionary gives E2by's exact instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and the registry shows it sitting beside E2Y and E2AY in the same table.
evidence_quote: In what kind of setting was the preschool / kindergarten program?
supersedes_rationale: The entry held only the question stem with no answer categories and the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that long day care is one of the coded settings.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E2y
variable_description: Whether the child attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. It is the gate for the rest of the preschool block: E2AY records the weekly hours and E2BY the setting, and both are answered only where this column records attendance. The dictionary describes it as the variable that identifies "if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school", and it was introduced in 2018 in place of the earlier E2 series of childcare and preschool items.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 1 for yes, 2 for no, and 88 for don't know. Introduced in 2018.
limitation: The coding is 1 for yes and 2 for no, unlike most AEDC yes/no items which use 0 and 1, so treating this as a 0/1 dummy turns every non-attender into an attender. It also does not carry back to earlier cycles: before 2018 the same information came from a different set of items, so an unadjusted trend from 2009 is not comparable.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording, the 2018 introduction, the 1/2/88 code list, and the conditional instructions on the dependent E2ay and E2by items.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child was in regular educational programs in the year before entering school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question stem alone with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it missed the unusual 1-for-yes, 2-for-no coding and the 2018 break in the series.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (long day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ay
variable_description: Whether the child was in long day care on a regular basis in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the first of six parallel columns, E3AY to E3FY, that cover long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative, a nanny and any other person, each coded the same way. Version 8.0 of the dictionary corrected the instruction on all six, recording that they are "asked to All" rather than only to children whose E2Y records a preschool program.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: No is coded 4, not 0, so a naive greater-than-zero test counts every non-attender as attending. Long day care here also overlaps with E2Y, because a long day care centre can deliver the preschool program reported there, so adding the E3 columns and E2Y together double counts the same child.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the five-code list and the version 8.0 correction to the filter, and the registry shows the six E3 columns sitting together in the same core table.
evidence_quote: E3ay – E3fy –correction to instruction, removed "only answer if E2y=yes" as these items are asked to All.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long question stem ending in 'long day care' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not show that 4 means no or that the filter was corrected in 2025.

value_domain: AEDC non-parental care intensity (family day care)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3by
variable_description: Whether the child was regularly in family day care in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. Family day care is the regulated home-based service, so this column separates it from the centre-based care in E3AY and from the informal relative care in E3CY and E3DY. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school", and the 2018 cycle rebuilt it from the earlier E2e and E2etime pair.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The full-time and part-time split is the only intensity information available, so it cannot yield hours, days per week or weeks of the year. Code 3 is a real answer rather than a missing value, and dropping it as missing biases any full-time share upwards.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the derivation from E2e and E2etime in 2018, and the five-code value list for this specific care type.
evidence_quote: To identify how often this child attended Family day care in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'family day care' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the five sibling columns or explained the intensity codes.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3cy
variable_description: Whether a grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. This is the largest of the informal care categories in Australia and the reason the E3 block distinguishes grandparents from other relatives, who are captured separately in E3DY. Because the columns are a multiple response set, a child can be recorded here and in the formal care columns E3AY and E3BY at the same time.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not say whether the grandparent lived with the child, was paid, or was the child's primary carer, so it cannot identify kinship care arrangements or grandparent-headed households. The teacher is answering about a household arrangement they did not observe, so the don't-know rate is a property of teacher knowledge rather than of the family.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the grandparent element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows the six-column multiple response block in one table.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with a Grandparent in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'grandparent' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record the intensity codes or that the six columns are a multiple response set.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3dy
variable_description: Whether a relative other than a parent or grandparent regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the residual family category in the E3 block: grandparents are taken out into E3CY, and unrelated carers fall to E3EY for a nanny or E3FY for a friend or neighbour. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying "if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school".
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: The relationship itself is not recorded, so an aunt, an adult sibling and a cousin all collapse into one code and no family structure can be reconstructed from it. It also cannot be read as a measure of family support, since a family with no relative nearby and a family that declined help both record 4.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code value list for the other relative element of the non-parental care question, and names the 2018 derivation from E2g and E2gtime.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another relative in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry held the shared question stem ending in 'other relative' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving the codes and the boundary against E3CY undocumented.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3ey
variable_description: Whether a nanny regularly cared for the child in the home in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It is the paid, unregulated, in-home category of the E3 block, distinct from the regulated home-based service captured in E3BY as family day care. Version 7.0 of the dictionary lists a correction to the field format and field values across E3ay to E3fy, so the published code list for this column is not identical in earlier dictionary releases.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It does not distinguish a live-in nanny from one who visits, or paid work from a reciprocal arrangement, so it cannot support any inference about household income. It is also a narrow category, so any subgroup estimate built on it should be checked against the AEDC suppression rules before it is reported.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the corrected five-code value list for the nanny element of the non-parental care question, and the version table records the field value correction covering E3ay to E3fy.
evidence_quote: Correction to field format/field values (PlaceOfBirth, B2-B7, C3-C51, E3ay-fy)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'nanny' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the published code list for this item had been corrected.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E3fy
variable_description: Whether someone outside the family, such as a friend or a neighbour, regularly cared for the child in the year before full-time school, and whether that care was full time or part time. It closes the E3 block as the catch-all: anything that was not long day care, family day care, a grandparent, another relative or a nanny lands here. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying care "with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school".
value_definition: A two-digit integer with five codes: 1 for yes full time, 2 for yes part time, 3 for yes but unsure whether full or part time, 4 for no, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: Being the residual category, it holds arrangements with nothing in common beyond not fitting the five named ones, so a positive value supports no statement about the type or quality of care. It is also the category a teacher is least likely to know about, so a low count here reflects reporting as much as behaviour.
rationale: The dictionary gives the item wording and the five-code list for the other person element of the non-parental care question, and the registry shows it as the last of the six parallel columns.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was in non-parental care with another person, such as a friend or neighbour, in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the shared stem ending in 'other (includes friend or neighbour)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so its role as the residual category and its code list were both missing.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E4
variable_description: Whether the child attended a playgroup at any point in the years before starting full-time school, as reported by the teacher. Its reference window is deliberately wider than the rest of the E block: E2Y and the E3 columns ask about the single year before school, while this one asks about "the years before entering full time school". The dictionary records that it was introduced in the 2012 cycle and renamed from E3b in 2015, so its name in older AEDC extracts is not E4.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with three codes: 0 for no, 1 for yes, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It records attendance ever, not how often or for how long, so a single visit and three years of weekly sessions are the same value. It also does not identify the type of playgroup, so supported and intensive playgroups aimed at families with additional needs cannot be separated from ordinary community ones.
rationale: The dictionary publishes E4 with the playgroup instrument text, the 0/1/88 code list, the 2012 introduction and the 2015 rename from E3b, matching the registry's own description of the column.
evidence_quote: To the best of your knowledge, has this child attended playgroup in the years before entering full time school
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the question wording alone with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no warning that the same concept appears as E3b in pre-2015 documentation.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E5
variable_description: The teacher's rating of how well the child is settling into school, asked as whether the child "is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school". It is one of three closing instrument questions, with E6 on parental engagement and E7 on reading at home, all sharing the same three-point scale. None of the three feed the five AEDC domain scores, so this column is an independent read on school transition rather than a component of the developmental measures.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is one teacher's global impression at a single point in the child's first school year, not a validated scale, so it cannot be treated as an outcome measure comparable to a domain score. The three points are ordinal and unequally spaced, so averaging them across a school or community produces a number with no defined unit.
rationale: The dictionary gives E5's instrument text, its purpose and its four-code value list, and section 3.1 sets out separately which items build the domain scores.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is making good progress in adapting to the structure and learning environment of the school
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Child is adapting to school' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the three-point rating scale and the 88 don't-know code were undocumented.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E6
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child's parents or caregivers are actively engaged with the school in supporting the child's learning. It is the school-side view of family involvement, and it pairs with E7, which asks about reading at home, to give two crude proxies for the home learning environment. The dictionary records that it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, a filter that was only lifted in 2015.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: New South Wales children are missing for the first two cycles, so a national trend that ignores this treats a coverage change as a real change in parental engagement. The rating also measures engagement visible to the school, so families who support learning at home without contacting the school score low on something they are doing.
rationale: The dictionary gives the instrument text, the four-code list, and an explicit note that the item was not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 with the filter revised in 2015.
evidence_quote: Not provided in New South Wales in Cycle 1/2
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Parents actively engaged with the school' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and omitted the New South Wales coverage gap that makes early-cycle national estimates wrong.

value_domain: AEDC three-point teacher rating (not true / somewhat true / very true)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section on Instrument variable E7
variable_description: The teacher's rating of whether the child is regularly read to, or encouraged in reading, at home. The question wording ends "as far as you can tell", which flags on the instrument itself that the teacher is inferring a home behaviour rather than observing it. Like E6, it was not collected in New South Wales in the 2009 and 2012 cycles, and the same three-point scale is used for both.
value_definition: A two-digit integer with four codes: 1 for not true, 2 for somewhat true, 3 for very true, and 88 for don't know.
limitation: It is a teacher's inference about the household, so it will partly track how much contact the family has with the school rather than what happens at home. Reading in a language other than English is not asked about separately, so a home rich in reading in another language can be rated as not true.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the instrument text including the 'as far as you can tell' qualifier, the four-code value list, and the New South Wales coverage note for Cycles 1 and 2.
evidence_quote: Would you say this child is regularly read to/encouraged in his/her reading at home as far as you can tell
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child is regularly read to at home' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the second-hand nature of the report nor the coverage gap was recorded.

value_domain: AEDC domain score, zero to ten
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: The child's score on emotional maturity, one of the five AEDC developmental domains, built from the teacher's answers to the emotional maturity items on the instrument. The dictionary states that for each domain "children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development", and that a score is only produced where at least 75 per cent of the domain's items were completed. EMOT_1 to EMOT_4 on the same row break it into prosocial and helping behaviour, anxious and fearful behaviour, aggressive behaviour, and hyperactive and inattentive behaviour, while EMOTCATEGORY converts the score into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.
value_definition: A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places. Higher is better, so the anxious, aggressive and hyperactive sub-domains are reverse scored before the domain score is formed.
limitation: The score cannot be reproduced from the item responses: the dictionary states the calculation methodologies are licensed from the Offord Centre for Child Studies and "are not available to the public". It is also a population measure, and the dictionary warns that AEDC indicators "have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children", so a single child's score is not a clinical result.
rationale: The dictionary defines EMOT as the derived emotional maturity domain score with a 7.4 numeric format, and section 3.1 gives the zero to ten range, the 75 per cent completion rule, the licensing of the calculation and the population-level caveat.
evidence_quote: For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Emotional maturity' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both value definition and limitation, so it did not even give the range of the score.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Which of four percentile bands the child's emotional maturity score falls into, where band 1 is the AEDC definition of developmentally vulnerable on this domain. The bands are 0 to 10th, 11th to 25th, 26th to 50th and 51st to 100th percentile, so band 1 is vulnerable, band 2 is at risk and bands 3 and 4 are on track. The cut-offs are fixed against the 2009 national collection: the dictionary states they "have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared".
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentile positions are those of the 2009 baseline distribution, adjusted for age variation across children in their first year of school.
limitation: The bands do not describe the current cohort, so a 12 per cent vulnerable rate in 2021 means 12 per cent scored below the 2009 tenth percentile, not that 12 per cent were in the bottom decile of 2021. The dictionary also states that domain indicator categories are not calculated for children diagnosed with special needs or aged under four, so their category is absent rather than high.
rationale: The dictionary gives EMOTCategory's four-band value list and section 3.1 explains that the cut-offs are anchored to the 2009 baseline and are not calculated for special needs children or children under four.
evidence_quote: The cut-off scores used in 2009 have remained the same across each collection cycle to provide a reference point against which later AEDC results can be compared.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Vulnerable - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which implied a yes/no flag when the column is in fact a four-band percentile grouping anchored to 2009.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child's emotional maturity result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. The dictionary defines a 1 as "Child does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", so a single flag folds three separate exclusions together. There is one of these per domain, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five a child is valid on.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for this domain; 1 otherwise.
limitation: A 0 does not tell you which of the three reasons applied, so it cannot be used to identify children with special needs or to measure teacher non-response. It is also domain specific, so a child can be valid on physical health and invalid on emotional maturity, and dropping every row with any invalid flag discards usable results on the other domains.
rationale: The dictionary gives the exact two-value list for EMOTValid, naming the three exclusion reasons that collapse into the 0 code, and documents the parallel per-domain flags and the VALIDDOMAINS counter.
evidence_quote: Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Valid - emotional maturity' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so a reader could not tell that special needs status and age three are folded into the same 0 as item non-response.

value_domain: AEDC English as a second language indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the teacher considers the child to have English as a second language, asked on the instrument as "Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)". It is one of three overlapping language columns and the most subjective: LANG asks whether a language other than English is spoken at home, and LBOTE is derived rather than asked. B1, the rating of the child's ability to use English effectively, sits alongside it and is the closer measure of proficiency.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes.
limitation: It is a teacher's classification, not a test, and it carries no threshold, so it varies with how each jurisdiction and school uses the label. A child can be ESL with fluent conversational English, and an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander child speaking Aboriginal English or Kriol may or may not be flagged depending on local practice, so an ESL rate cannot be read as an English proficiency rate.
rationale: The dictionary publishes ESL as an instrument item with its exact question wording and a 0/1 value list, and documents Lang, LBOTE and B1 as the separate language variables it is often confused with.
evidence_quote: Is the child considered ESL (English as a second language)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'ESL (english as a second language)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it restated the acronym and never distinguished the column from LANG or LBOTE.

value_domain: AEDC child sex or gender code
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: The child's sex or gender as recorded through the school enrolment process and carried onto the AEDC instrument. The dictionary describes the data element as "The sex of the child" while giving its purpose as identifying the child's gender, which reflects a change made in 2024 when the instrument item was relabelled from sex to gender and expanded beyond a binary. Codes 1 for male and 2 for female carry every cycle, so which codes can occur depends on the collection year of the row.

value_domain: Count of AEDC domains in the top percentile band
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables

variable_description: Whether AEDC results for this child's Indigenous Region are publishable, and if not, which rule blocked them. The codes separate three distinct failures: fewer than fifteen valid AEDC children, fewer than two teachers, and the coverage rule that at least 80 per cent of non-special-needs children in the area were assessed. It is the same six-code scheme used by LGAPUBLIC, IAREPUBLIC, ILOCPUBLIC and the SA2 and SA3 equivalents, so one reading of the codes serves the whole family.

The dictionary records a field length of 1 even though the suppression codes run to two digits.
limitation: It governs public reporting of the area, not the record in front of you, so a child in a region coded 21 still carries full domain scores in the microdata. Code 9 is a different problem from the rest: it says the child's location could not be resolved to a region at all, so filtering it out removes children with missing geography rather than children in small areas.
rationale: The dictionary prints the six-code reportability list for IREGPublic and repeats the identical scheme for the other geography levels, which is what makes the codes readable as suppression reasons.
evidence_quote: IREG not public: Less than 15 AEDC children valid and less than two teachers
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Indigenous region publishable' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column distinguishes small counts, too few teachers, a coverage failure and missing geography.

variable_description: The campus code the state or territory education authority uses for the campus the child was assessed at. The dictionary defines it as "The individual campus code used by the jurisdiction to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC" and states that it is unique within jurisdiction and year. LOCATIONAGEID on the same row is the Australian Government's code for the same campus, and SCHOOLID is the school the campus belongs to.
