It is also suppressed for schools outside a data recipient's jurisdiction, so it is systematically blank rather than missing at random.
rationale: The dictionary gives JCampusID's definition, its five-digit format, the explicit uniqueness rule and the suppression instruction, and lists it beside the Australian Government campus identifiers.
evidence_quote: Unique within jurisdiction and year
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Jurisdictional campus identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not warn that the code repeats across states and across years.

value_domain: AEDC language other than English at home indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the child speaks a language other than English at home, asked on the instrument as "Does the child speak a language other than English at home". It is the gate for the whole language block: LANGUAGEID, ILANGUAGEID, CANCOM and the LANGSOURCE columns all carry the instruction "Only answer if Lang = Yes", so a blank in those columns means the question was never put rather than that the child speaks only English. ESL and LBOTE are the two related flags, and neither is the same measure.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes.
limitation: It records home use, not proficiency in either language, so it cannot distinguish a child fluent in two languages from one with little English; CANCOM and B1 answer that. Because it filters the rest of the language block, treating a blank LANGUAGEID as English-speaking silently converts a skip into an observation.
rationale: The dictionary gives Lang's exact instrument text and 0/1 value list, and prints the 'Only answer if Lang = Yes' instruction on CanCom, LanguageID and each LangSource column, which establishes the filter structure.
evidence_quote: Does the child speak a language other than English at home
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Speaks language other than english' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no indication that this column controls whether the rest of the language block is answered at all.

value_domain: AEDC domain score, zero to ten
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: The child's score on the language and cognitive skills domain, which the AEDC qualifies as school-based because the items ask what the teacher observes the child doing in the classroom. LANGCOG_1 to LANGCOG_4 on the same row split it into basic literacy, interest in literacy and numeracy and memory, advanced literacy, and basic numeracy. Like the other four domains it runs from zero to ten with higher scores meaning stronger development, and LANGCOGCATEGORY turns it into the vulnerable, at risk and on track bands.
value_definition: A continuous numeric value from 0 to 10, stored with four decimal places, formed from the domain's instrument items where at least 75 per cent of them were completed.
limitation: It is measured through classroom English, so a child with strong literacy and numeracy in another language can score low on skills they hold; the domain is not a test administered to the child. The derivation is also closed, since the dictionary states the domain score methodologies are licensed intellectual property and not available to the public, so the score cannot be recomputed or audited from the item columns.
rationale: The dictionary defines LANGCOG as the derived school-based language and cognitive skills domain score with a 7.4 numeric format, and section 3.1 gives the zero to ten range, the completion rule and the licensing restriction.
evidence_quote: To identify the child's (school-based) language and cognitive skills domain score.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Language and cognitive skills' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so neither the range, the four sub-domains, nor the school-based qualification was recorded.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 3.1 Domain Indicators and section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Which of four percentile bands the child's language and cognitive skills score falls into, with band 1 marking developmental vulnerability on this domain. Band 2 is the at risk group, and bands 3 and 4 are both on track, which is why the published on track figure combines them. The dictionary notes that the cut-offs "take into account the age variations in the population of children in their first year of schooling", so the bands are age adjusted rather than raw score thresholds.
value_definition: A one-digit integer with four codes: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th, all positioned against the 2009 national baseline.
limitation: Because the boundaries are age adjusted and anchored to 2009, two children with the same LANGCOG score can sit in different bands, so the category cannot be reconstructed by ranking the score column. Children with a special needs diagnosis and children aged three receive no category, so their rows are blank rather than in band 4.
rationale: The dictionary prints the four-band value list for LANGCOGCategory and section 3.1 states that the cut-offs are age adjusted, fixed to the 2009 baseline, and not applied to special needs children or children under four.
evidence_quote: Domain cut-offs take into account the age variations in the population of children in their first year of schooling.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Vulnerable - language and cognition' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which read as a binary flag and hid both the four bands and the age adjustment.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 15 AEDC Domain Variables
variable_description: Whether the child's language and cognitive skills result counts as valid for AEDC reporting. A 0 means the child has special needs status, is three years old, or left too many of this domain's instrument questions unanswered; a 1 means none of those applied. It is the language and cognition member of a set of five, one per domain, and VALIDINSTRUMENT separately identifies children with fewer than four valid domain scores for the 80 per cent coverage rule.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 where the domain result is not valid, 1 where it is. The item threshold behind it is the 75 per cent domain completion rule.
limitation: It is a reporting eligibility flag, not a data quality score, so a 1 does not mean every question was answered and a 0 does not mean the teacher failed to respond. Because the same 0 covers special needs status, it is not safe to use this column as a proxy for teacher non-response on the language items.
rationale: The dictionary gives LANGCOGValid's exact two-value list naming the three exclusion reasons, and documents ValidInstrument and ValidDomains as the separate coverage variables.
evidence_quote: To identify the validity of the child's results on the language and cognitive skills (school-based) domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Valid - language and cognitive skills' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never named the three conditions that produce a 0.

value_domain: AEDC information source selection (three-valued multiple response)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the teacher relied on a written record, meaning an enrolment form, an assessment or a report, when answering CANCOM about the child's ability to communicate in the home language. It is the documentary option in a six-way multiple response set, LANGSOURCE0 to LANGSOURCE5, that records where the teacher's answer came from. The whole set is answered only where LANG records a language other than English at home.

value_domain: AEDC language background other than English indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 10 Demographic Variables
variable_description: Whether the child has a language background other than English, derived by the AEDC rather than asked of the teacher. It is the third and broadest of the AEDC language flags, and the dictionary prints the rule that builds it: "Children are considered 'LBOTE' if they speak a language other than English at home, or if they speak English at home but are still considered to have ESL (English as a second language) status." It is therefore the union of LANG and ESL, which is why it is always at least as large as either one on its own. The dictionary lists it among the variables whose names, descriptions or notes were corrected in the 2024 revision, so its published definition is not identical across dictionary versions.
value_definition: A one-digit integer flag: 0 for no, 1 for yes, with the source given as derived rather than instrument. It equals 1 where LANG is 1 or ESL is 1.
limitation: Because it is the union of two flags it cannot be read as either one: an LBOTE rate counts children who speak only English at home but are classed ESL by the teacher, so it inherits the subjectivity of the ESL judgement. Language background is also not proficiency, so an LBOTE rate is not a measure of how many children need English language support.
rationale: The dictionary gives LBOTE as a derived 0/1 indicator distinct from the instrument-collected Lang and ESL items, and names it in the version 7.0 list of variables whose descriptions were corrected.
evidence_quote: To indicate if the child has a Language Background Other Than English (LBOTE).
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the acronym as 'LBOTE indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither expanded the abbreviation nor recorded that the column is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: ABS SEIFA Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage score
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 4.2 SEIFA and section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The ABS socio-economic index score for the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, used as the standard area measure of disadvantage in AEDC analysis. The dictionary is explicit about which index: "In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD)". The Census vintage behind the score changes by cycle, being 2006 for the 2009 collection, 2011 for 2012 and 2015, 2016 for 2018 and 2021 for the 2021 and 2024 collections. LCABSSEIFACATEGORY beside it groups the same score into ordinal bands.
value_definition: A numeric value stored with four decimal places, on the ABS IRSD scale that is standardised to a national mean near 1000. Where a local community spans more than one SEIFA area, the score is a population-weighted average of the component scores.
limitation: It describes an area, not a family, so using it as a child-level measure of household disadvantage is an ecological inference and will understate the spread within a community. The IRSD also measures disadvantage only, and the ABS warns it is not a measure of advantage, so a high score means an absence of disadvantage rather than affluence; and because the Census vintage changes between cycles, part of any movement in the score is a change of index rather than a change of the place.
rationale: The dictionary names the specific SEIFA index the AEDC uses, prints the cycle-by-cycle table of SEIFA vintages for local community scores, and explains the population-weighted recalculation used where boundaries split.
evidence_quote: In AEDC, we use the Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage (IRSD).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community seifa score' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say which of the four SEIFA indexes was used, nor that the vintage differs by collection cycle.

value_domain: ABS local government area code (local community based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The local government area associated with the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, as distinct from the LGA the child's own address falls in. The dictionary keeps two parallel geography blocks for exactly this reason: the child based block holds LGACODE, and the local community based block holds this column. It was introduced in the 2012 cycle, and LCLGANAME beside it carries the readable label.
value_definition: A five-digit integer on the ABS local government area classification for the edition in force in the cycle, attached to the local community rather than to the child.
limitation: AEDC Local Community boundaries are built on ABS statistical areas, not on council boundaries, so a local community can straddle two councils and this column then names only the one it is associated with. Using it in place of LGACODE therefore assigns some children to a council area they do not live in.
rationale: The dictionary defines LCLGACode as the local government area code associated with the Local Community, in a section separate from the child based LGACode, and section 4.1 explains that local community boundaries are aligned to SA1 building blocks.
evidence_quote: Local Government Area code associated with the Local Community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Local community lga code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish the column from the child based LGACODE, which is the confusion that matters.

value_domain: ABS local government area name (local community based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography
variable_description: The written name of the local government area associated with the child's AEDC Local Community, the label for LCLGACODE. It is held in a longer field than the child based LGANAME, at forty characters against thirty, so the two columns can render the same council differently. It was introduced with LCLGACODE in the 2012 cycle.
value_definition: Left-justified text up to 40 characters, carrying the ABS local government area name for the edition in force in the cycle.
limitation: Council names change with amalgamations and de-amalgamations, so matching AEDC cycles on this text rather than on the code drops or mismatches records for every council that was renamed. Council names are also not unique across states, so a national join on name alone merges unrelated areas.
rationale: The dictionary gives LCLGAName as a 40-character text field paired with LCLGACode in the local community geography section, and gives LGAName a 30-character field in the child based section, which establishes the differing field widths.
evidence_quote: Local Government Area name associated with the Local Community.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community lga name' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, offering no field length and no reason to prefer the code as a join key.

value_domain: ABS local government area code (child based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography
variable_description: The local government area the child lives in, coded on the ABS classification and assigned from the child's own address rather than from the school's. It belongs to the child based geography block, which also holds the SA2, SA3, SA4, GCCSA, remoteness and Indigenous geography columns for the same address. It was introduced in the 2012 cycle, and LGAPUBLIC on the same row says whether AEDC results for that LGA are publishable.
value_definition: A five-digit integer on the ABS local government area classification, with the code list published in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables for the ASGS edition in force in the cycle.
limitation: It is not present for the 2009 cycle, since the column began in 2012, so a panel across all cycles has a structural gap rather than missing values. ABS reissues local government area codes annually, so the same council can carry different codes in different cycles and a code alone is not interpretable without the collection year.
rationale: The dictionary gives LGACode as a five-digit child based geography introduced in 2012, with values referred to the reference tables, and lists it beside the other ASGS geographies assigned to the child's address.
evidence_quote: A local government area code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'LGA code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, restating the abbreviation and omitting both the 2012 start and the separate local community LGA column it is easily confused with.

value_domain: ABS local government area name (child based)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography
variable_description: The written name of the local government area the child lives in, the label attached to LGACODE. It is a thirty-character field, which is shorter than the forty characters used for the local community equivalent LCLGANAME, so longer council names can appear cut differently in the two columns. Like the code, it starts in the 2012 cycle.
value_definition: Left-justified text up to 30 characters, taking ABS local government area names from the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables for the edition in force in the cycle.
limitation: Thirty characters is short enough to truncate long council names, so the text is not always a complete name and is unsafe as a display label without checking. Names are also not unique nationally, so grouping by this column alone merges same-named councils in different states.
rationale: The dictionary gives LGAName as a 30-character text field in the child based geography section with values referred to the reference tables, alongside the 40-character LCLGAName in the local community section.
evidence_quote: A local government area name.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'LGA name' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, giving no field length and no warning about truncation or duplicate names.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 11 Child Based Geography
variable_description: Whether AEDC results for the child's local government area can be published, and which rule blocked them if not. Code 1 means results are publicly available; codes 21, 22 and 23 mark small counts, fewer than two teachers, or both; code 5 marks a failure of the 80 per cent coverage rule; and code 9 means the location itself could not be determined. It uses the same six-code scheme as IREGPUBLIC, IAREPUBLIC, ILOCPUBLIC and the SA2 and SA3 publishability columns.
value_definition: An integer with six codes: 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 and 23, where 1 is publishable and the others each name a reason the area's results are withheld from public reporting. The dictionary records a field length of 1 even though the suppression codes run to two digits.
limitation: It constrains public reporting of the area, not access to the record, so children in an area coded 22 still carry full domain scores in the microdata and can be analysed. Reading anything other than 1 as missing data conflates a genuinely missing geography, code 9, with areas whose data exists but is too thin to publish.
rationale: The dictionary prints the full six-code reportability list for LGAPublic with the wording of each suppression reason, and repeats the same scheme across the other geography levels.
evidence_quote: LGA not public: Less than 80% of all non-special needs children
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'LGA publishable' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which suggested a yes/no flag when the column in fact carries six codes distinguishing four different suppression reasons.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 12 Local Community Based Geography and section 4.1 Changes to the AEDC geography
variable_description: The code for the AEDC Local Community the child lives in, the smallest of the four levels the AEDC reports at, below Community, state or territory and national. It is the key for the whole local community block on the row: LOCALCOMMUNITY holds the name, LCLGACODE the associated council, LCABSSEIFASCORE the area disadvantage score, and LCPUBLIC whether the community's results can be published. The boundaries are drawn to align with ABS Statistical Area Level 1 building blocks so that AEDC results can be compared with Census data.
value_definition: A six-digit derived integer, with the code list published in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables.
limitation: The identifier is not stable in meaning across releases: new local community boundaries were created in 2015 to align with the ASGS, and revised boundaries were introduced for the 2024 collection and applied retrospectively to all earlier cycles, so the same community can cover a different area than it did in an earlier extract. The dictionary warns that a community may keep its name while its geography changes, so neither the code nor the name guarantees a like-for-like comparison over time.
rationale: The dictionary gives LocalCommunityID as a six-digit derived code with a 2015 revision note, and section 4.1 documents the retrospective boundary revision applied for the 2024 collection and its effect on comparability.
evidence_quote: Whilst AEDC Local Communities and Communities may have the same name as in previous collections, the geographical area covered may have changed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Local community identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not record that the boundaries behind the identifier have been redrawn twice and applied retrospectively.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary (Version 8.0, October 2025), Australian Government Department of Education, section 8 Pre-Instrument Variables
variable_description: The Australian Government's national code for the campus the child was assessed at, defined by the dictionary as "The individual campus code used by the Australian Government to identify each school campus participating in the AEDC". It was introduced in the 2021 collection to replace AGCampusID, and both were in use during that cycle before AGCampusID was discontinued in 2024. It is the national counterpart to JCAMPUSID, which is the jurisdiction's own code for the same campus.
value_definition: A five-digit integer allocated nationally by the Australian Government. Introduced in the 2021 cycle and renamed from AGLocationID in 2024.
limitation: It identifies a campus, not a school, so a multi-campus school has several values and counting distinct values here overstates the number of schools; SCHOOLID is the school-level key. Because it starts in 2021 and overlapped with AGCampusID in that cycle, a campus panel built on this column alone loses every earlier cycle and can double count 2021 campuses carrying both identifiers.
rationale: The dictionary gives LocationAGEID's definition, five-digit format and 2021 introduction, and the AGCampusID entry records that it was replaced by AGLocationID in 2021 with both in use that year and fully discontinued in 2024.
evidence_quote: Item was replaced by AGLocationID in 2021 (both were in use in the 2021 AEDC collection)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's phrase 'National campus identifier used by deewr' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not record the 2021 start, the rename, or the campus against school distinction.

value_domain: Count of AEDC domains in the vulnerable band (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'LowTotal'
variable_description: A count, from zero to five, of the developmental domains on which the child scored in the bottom tenth of the 2009 national distribution. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the number of domains in which the child is in the 0 to 10th percentile category", so it is the number of the five category columns - PHYSCATEGORY, SOCCATEGORY, EMOTCATEGORY, LANGCOGCATEGORY and COMGENCATEGORY - that equal 1. HIGHTOTAL is its mirror at the other end of the distribution, and the published summary indicators DV1 and DV2 are yes/no readings of this same count.
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The cut-off for each domain is the tenth percentile of the 2009 AEDC population and has been held fixed at that baseline for every cycle since, so the count is measured against 2009 children rather than against the child's own cohort.
limitation: It does not say which domains, so two children both counted at two can be vulnerable on entirely different pairs and only the five category columns separate them. A domain that could not be scored is simply not counted, which means a low value can mean strong development or missing information; VALIDDOMAINS and TOTALMISS are what tell those apart.
rationale: The AEDC Data Dictionary publishes LowTotal as a derived variable with an explicit purpose statement naming the percentile band, and the surrounding category and validity columns in the PLIDA core tables show exactly what it is summing.
evidence_quote: To identify the number of domains in which the child is in the 0 to 10th percentile category.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's line 'Number of domains in which child is vulnerable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said what 'vulnerable' means numerically or that the cut-off is frozen at 2009.

value_domain: Month of AvEDI completion (April to August)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'MOC' and section 4.4
variable_description: The calendar month in which the teacher completed the child's Australian version of the Early Development Instrument. Collection runs in the first half of the school year, so the dictionary allows only five values, April through August, and the field is a single digit rather than a date. With YEAR it dates the assessment, and it is half of the age calculation: the dictionary says AEDC age "is based on the student's reported date of birth and the date on which the Instrument was completed by the teacher".
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 4 April, 5 May, 6 June, 7 July, 8 August. There is no day component and no value outside that window.
limitation: It cannot order two assessments inside the same month, and it is not an enrolment date or a data-supply date. It is also not a neutral stamp: the dictionary says the domain cut-offs take account of age variation among children in their first year of school, but says nothing about time already spent at school, so an April child and an August child can differ on months of schooling in a way the published method does not address.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element description, the five permitted values and, in section 4.4, the role the completion date plays in deriving age, which is the fact a user of the age columns needs.
evidence_quote: The calendar month in which the Instrument was completed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Month instrument completed' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which hid that the field is a bare month number confined to April-August and that it feeds the age derivation.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack0' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on none of the five AEDC domains, held only for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles. It is the one member of the legacy ONTRACK series with no modern successor: the dictionary records that ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 were rebuilt to the OT5 method and reissued as OT1 to OT4, but that "OnTrack on no domains (OnTrack0) was not updated to the new methodology". A six-cycle series of children on track nowhere therefore has to be built from the five domain category columns instead.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns rather than reported by a teacher.
limitation: It carries no denominator flag of the kind OT1FLAG to OT5FLAG provide, so children whose domains could not be scored sit in the same value as children who were assessed and fell short everywhere. It is also not the complement of a published AEDC figure: the dictionary names only DV1, DV2 and OT5 as summary indicators, and an on-track-on-no-domains rate is not among them.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element and, in the 2024 changes section, states directly that this one variable was left on the old calculation while its siblings were replaced, which is the fact that decides how it can be used.
evidence_quote: OnTrack on no domains (OnTrack0) was not updated to the new methodology.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only 'On track on no domains' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell it is a legacy column confined to the first three cycles and deliberately not modernised.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack1' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on at least one of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only. It is the superseded form of OT1: the dictionary records that ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 "have been recalculated to align with the methodology for calculating OT5", which produced OT1 to OT4 and a denominator flag for each. That is why the old and new names never appear in the same cycle table.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns.
limitation: Stacking this column for 2009 to 2015 onto OT1 for 2018 to 2024 creates a break that looks like a change in children: OT1 is reported over the OT1FLAG denominator and this column has no denominator rule at all. Being on track on one domain also says nothing about the other four, so it can be 1 for a child LOWTOTAL shows as vulnerable on three.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element description and, in section 6, states that this variable was recalculated into OT1, which is the only fact that makes the two columns comparable or not.
evidence_quote: legacy variables OnTrack1, OnTrack2, OnTrack3 and OnTrack4 variables have been recalculated to align with the methodology for calculating OT5
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'On track on one or more domains' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and so said nothing about the 2024 recalculation that makes this column non-comparable with OT1.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack2' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, carried in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables. The dictionary describes it as "On track on two or more domains" and lists it as a Master unit record file variable introduced in 2009, before the AEDC had settled on a single strengths measure. From 2018 the equivalent is OT2, calculated on the aligned method and reported over the OT2FLAG denominator.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived by counting the domains whose category column places the child above the 25th percentile.
limitation: No AEDC national report publishes a two-or-more on-track rate, so a figure taken from this column has nothing published to check it against. It is also not the opposite of DV2, vulnerable on two or more domains: a child can be on track on two domains and vulnerable on two others, so both columns can read 1 for the same child.
rationale: The dictionary carries the element and the 2024 change note that replaced it with OT2, and section 3.2 lists which summary indicators the AEDC actually reports, which is what tells a reader this threshold is not one of them.
evidence_quote: On track on two or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say the column is a legacy series with no published counterpart.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack3' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, held for the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify if the child is developmentally on track on three or more domains", and its cumulative thresholds mean it is implied by ONTRACK4 and ONTRACK5 on the same row. OT3 is the 2018-onward replacement, built on the aligned method.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The ONTRACK series is cumulative, so a child flagged here is also flagged on ONTRACK1 and ONTRACK2.
limitation: The gap between this column and ONTRACK4 is the share on track on exactly three domains only because the legacy series shares one unrestricted denominator; the same subtraction on OT3 and OT4 is not safe, because those carry separate qualification flags. Three of five is also not a milestone the AEDC defines - the cut-offs are per domain, so the count has no interpretation beyond arithmetic.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element and the change note explaining that the modern OT series introduced per-indicator denominator flags that the legacy series lacks, which is what governs whether thresholds can be differenced.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on three or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's phrase with the duplicated generic sentence, so it neither placed the column in the legacy series nor warned about mixing it with the OT columns.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack4' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify if the child is developmentally on track on four or more domains", one step below the all-five threshold that became the AEDC's national strengths indicator. It was recalculated into OT4 for the 2024 collection and the PLIDA files carry OT4 from 2018 onward in its place.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns.
limitation: It is not the complement of DV1: a child on track on four domains and vulnerable on the fifth reads 1 here and 1 on DV1 at the same time, so the two cannot be used as opposite ends of one scale. Nor is it a near-miss version of ONTRACK5, since the domain a child falls short on is not recorded here and only the category columns show it.
rationale: The dictionary carries the element and section 3.2 sets out how the vulnerability and strengths indicators relate, which establishes that the two are not complements.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on four or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice and offered no warning that a child can be flagged here and still be developmentally vulnerable.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Ontrack5' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
variable_description: A yes/no marker that the child was developmentally on track on all five domains, on the calculation used up to the 2015 cycle. This is the measure the Productivity Commission adopted in 2018 for the Closing the Gap target on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children thriving in their early years, which is why it was singled out for rebuilding: the dictionary records a decision "to re-calculate the On Track on 5 domains (OnTrack5) to align with the Vulnerability Summary Indicators (DV1 and DV2)" made in 2021, producing OT5 and OT5FLAG. In PLIDA this column covers 2009 to 2015 and the new pair covers 2018 to 2024.
value_definition: A single-digit integer flag, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Like the other summary indicators it has no score and no cut-off of its own, resting on the five domain category columns.
limitation: Figures built from this column do not reproduce the 2021 National Report or the Closing the Gap tracking, which use OT5 over the OT5FLAG denominator; the dictionary is explicit that the new variables "need to be used to replicate the figures". Treating the old and new columns as one continuous series therefore puts an artificial step at the 2018 boundary.
rationale: Appendix 3 of the dictionary documents in full why this variable was recalculated, what replaced it and which version reproduces published national figures.
evidence_quote: the new variables (OT5 and OT5Flag) are considered as the national summary indicators and need to be used to replicate the figures in the 2021 AEDC National Report and the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap target tracking
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'On track on five domains' with the duplicated generic sentence, hiding both its role in the Closing the Gap target and the fact that it was superseded by a differently calculated column.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1' and section 6
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on one or more of the five domains, calculated on the same basis as the vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2. The dictionary defines it as "On Track - On one or more domain" and records it as introduced for the 2024 collection, when the legacy ONTRACK1 to ONTRACK4 columns were recalculated; PLIDA carries it from the 2018 cycle, so the rebuilt series has been applied back across the earlier files. A rate from this column has to be taken over children with OT1FLAG equal to 1.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. It is derived from the five domain category columns; the summary indicators carry no score and no cut-off of their own.
limitation: One or more domains on track is a very low bar and is not the AEDC's headline strengths measure, which is OT5 across all five. Reading a high rate here as good news inverts the intent, because the indicator is passed by a child who is developmentally vulnerable on the other four domains.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element, its purpose, its permitted values and the 2024 change note that created it out of the legacy ONTRACK1 column, and section 3.2 explains why the summary indicators have no score.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on one or more domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not mention OT1FLAG, without which the column produces a number that is not the published rate.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on two or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On two or more domains". It is one of the four sub-threshold companions to OT5, created in 2024 so the whole on-track ladder is calculated the way the national indicators are, and it is reported over the OT2FLAG denominator rather than over all rows. The 2009 to 2015 files hold the older ONTRACK2 in its place.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from how many of the five domain category columns place the child above the 25th percentile.
limitation: The AEDC publishes no two-or-more on-track rate, so a figure from this column cannot be checked against a national report. It is also not the mirror of DV2: DV2 counts vulnerability on two or more domains, and a child can be flagged on both columns at once.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its purpose and its values, and section 3.2 lists the three indicators the AEDC actually reports, which does not include this threshold.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on two or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line with the duplicated generic sentence, so it neither named the denominator flag nor warned that the column has no published counterpart.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on three or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On three or more domains". It sits in the middle of the OT1 to OT5 ladder introduced for the 2024 collection, and like the rest of that ladder it is meant to be averaged only over children whose matching flag, OT3FLAG, equals 1. Its 2009 to 2015 predecessor is ONTRACK3.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. The thresholds are cumulative, so a child flagged on OT4 or OT5 is also flagged here.
limitation: Subtracting the OT4 rate from the OT3 rate does not give the share on track on exactly three domains, because OT3FLAG and OT4FLAG are separate columns that need not qualify the same children. Nor does the count carry a developmental meaning - each domain has its own cut-off, so moving from three to four is not a fixed increment of development.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element and a separate denominator flag entry for each threshold, which is what establishes that thresholds cannot be differenced without checking the flags.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on three or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording with the generic sentence printed twice, so it gave no hint that each threshold carries its own denominator rule.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4'
variable_description: A yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on four or more of the five domains, defined by the dictionary as "On Track - On four or more domains". It is the closest threshold below OT5, the AEDC's national strengths indicator, and it was created in 2024 when the legacy ONTRACK columns were recalculated onto the OT5 method. Rates need the OT4FLAG denominator.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no, derived from the five domain category columns rather than from a score.
limitation: It is not the opposite of DV1: a child on track on four domains and developmentally vulnerable on the fifth reads 1 on both columns, so the pair cannot be treated as two ends of one scale. It also does not identify which domain the child fell short on, which only the five category columns show.
rationale: The dictionary carries the element and its purpose, and section 3.2 describes the vulnerability and strengths indicators as separate measures rather than complements.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child is developmentally on track on four or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, leaving the reader to assume wrongly that a child on track on four domains cannot be counted as developmentally vulnerable.

value_domain: AEDC On Track on Five national summary indicator (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5' and section 3.2
variable_description: The AEDC's national strengths measure: a yes/no indicator that the child was developmentally on track on every one of the five domains. The dictionary calls it the third summary indicator and describes it as "a strength-based indicator" beside the two vulnerability indicators DV1 and DV2, and it was created in 2021 so that the strengths measure would be calculated the same way they are. It is the variable behind the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking, and rates must be taken over children with OT5FLAG equal to 1.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Like the vulnerability indicators it has no score and no cut-off of its own, resting on whether the child is on track on each domain separately.
limitation: It is not the opposite of DV1. A child who is at risk rather than vulnerable on one domain reads 0 here and 0 on DV1, so the two indicators leave a middle group neither counts and one minus the OT5 rate is not the vulnerability rate. Results from 2018 onward also cannot be joined to ONTRACK5 in the 2009 to 2015 files, which uses the superseded calculation.
rationale: The dictionary defines the element, section 3.2 sets out its status as one of three national summary indicators and explains that summary indicators carry no score, and Appendix 3 records why it replaced ONTRACK5.
evidence_quote: The third summary indicator, On Track on Five domains (OT5) is a strength-based indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Child is developmentally on track on all five domains' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and so omitted the denominator flag, the 2021 recalculation and the break with ONTRACK5.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT1Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child counts in the denominator when an on-track-on-one-or-more rate is worked out. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT1" and its purpose as identifying whether the child qualifies for that calculation; AEDC summary indicators are published as percentages of qualifying children, not of every row on the file. It is the strengths-side equivalent of DV1FLAG, and filtering on it before averaging OT1 is the difference between the published rate and a number that merely resembles it.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It does not say why a child was excluded. The AEDC's exclusion rules cover children with diagnosed special needs, children aged three and children with too many unanswered instrument items, and all three land on the same zero, so SPECIALNEEDS, the age columns and the five domain validity columns are needed to tell them apart.
rationale: The dictionary publishes a separate flag element for each on-track threshold with its own purpose statement, and the domain validity entries give the exclusion rules the flags implement.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on one or more domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long phrase with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained what a denominator flag is for or what a zero can mean.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT2Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-two-or-more rate. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT2", introduced in 2024 alongside OT2 itself when the legacy ONTRACK series was rebuilt with explicit denominators. Each on-track threshold has its own flag, so this one qualifies a child for OT2 and for nothing else.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: A denominator flag is not a data-quality flag for the whole row. A child excluded here can still have usable domain scores, geography and demographics, so dropping records on this flag discards analysis that has nothing to do with the summary indicator.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the flag as its own data element with a purpose limited to the OT2 calculation, which establishes both its role and its narrow scope.
evidence_quote: Qualifies for the denominator of OT2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's sentence with the generic no-value-list line twice, so it did not distinguish a denominator rule from a record-level quality flag.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT3Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-three-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT3". It was introduced for the 2024 collection with OT3, part of giving every on-track threshold the kind of explicit denominator the vulnerability indicators had carried since 2009. Without it, an average of OT3 runs over children the AEDC does not count.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It qualifies the child for one threshold only, so a denominator built once from this column and reused across OT1 to OT5 will not reproduce the published rates. The dictionary does not publish the qualification rule behind it either, so the flag has to be read from the file rather than rebuilt from the five domain validity columns.
rationale: The dictionary gives each threshold its own flag element with its own purpose, which is the evidence that the flags are not interchangeable.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on three or more domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, so a reader could reasonably have assumed one flag serves all the on-track columns.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT4Flag'
variable_description: Marks whether the child belongs in the denominator of the on-track-on-four-or-more rate, defined by the dictionary as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT4". It is one of the four flags added in 2024 when OT1 to OT4 were created, modelled on DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG so that every AEDC indicator states who it is calculated over. It applies to OT4 only.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It is not interchangeable with DV1FLAG or DV2FLAG. The strengths and vulnerability denominators were aligned in method rather than merged, so each indicator keeps its own flag and a single 'valid children' total cannot serve both families of indicators.
rationale: Appendix 3 explains that the strengths indicator was recalculated to align with the vulnerability indicators, and the dictionary still lists a separate flag element for each, which shows alignment did not mean a shared denominator column.
evidence_quote: Qualifies for the denominator of OT4.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's phrase with the generic sentence twice and gave no warning against reusing the vulnerability denominators for the strengths indicators.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'OT5Flag' and Appendix 3 section A2.1.1
variable_description: Marks whether the child counts in the denominator of the on-track-on-all-five rate, the AEDC's national strengths indicator. The dictionary defines it as "Qualifies for the denominator of OT5" and records it as created in 2021 with OT5 itself, so that the strengths measure would carry the same kind of qualification rule as DV1FLAG and DV2FLAG. It is the flag the Productivity Commission's Closing the Gap tracking rests on, so an OT5 rate calculated without it will not match the published series.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no.
limitation: It is not a general statement that the child has five usable domain scores; that is what VALIDDOMAINS counts. Applying it to a different indicator, or applying it after averaging rather than before, changes the number away from the published one.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the flag element and Appendix 3 explains that refining the denominator was the whole reason the OT5 pair was created, which is what makes the flag load-bearing rather than incidental.
evidence_quote: To identify if the child qualifies for the denominator for the calculation of developmentally on track on all five domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the national strengths figure is defined by this flag.

value_domain: Gender of first listed parent or carer (school enrolment)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Gender'
variable_description: The recorded gender of the adult listed first on the child's school enrolment, pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument. It identifies whichever adult the school listed first, which need not be a mother, a birth parent or an adult living with the child. With PARENT2GENDER it is the only signal in the AEDC core file about the adults around the child, and it appears from the 2018 cycle onward.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. There is no non-binary category and no code separating a refusal from an unrecorded value.
limitation: It cannot identify family structure. A missing PARENT2GENDER can mean one adult on the enrolment form, a school that recorded only one contact, or a second adult whose details were withheld, and none of those is the same as a single-parent household.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its three permitted values and, crucially, that the source is pre-population from school enrolment rather than the AEDC instrument, which is what limits how the column can be read.
evidence_quote: Gender of first parent or carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'First parent or carer gender' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the value comes from the enrolment record or that 'parent 1' is only an ordering on a form.

value_domain: Gender of second listed parent or carer (school enrolment)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Gender'
variable_description: The recorded gender of the second adult on the child's school enrolment, present only where the school listed a second parent or carer. Like the first-parent column it is pre-populated from enrolment rather than collected by the AEDC, so it follows whatever the school held rather than the child's living arrangements when the instrument was completed. Paired with PARENT1GENDER it is sometimes used to approximate two-parent or same-sex households, which the AEDC does not itself measure.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Male, 2 Female, 9 Not stated. The value is absent rather than zero where no second adult was recorded.
limitation: This is the weakest basis in the file for inferring household type: a 9 and an absent second parent look similar in analysis but mean different things, and neither confirms who lived with the child. The AEDC records no relationship, so 'parent or carer 2' can be a grandparent, a step-parent or another guardian.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with the same three values as the first-parent column and records its source as pre-population, which establishes both the coding and the reason a gap is ambiguous.
evidence_quote: Gender of second parent or carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Second parent or carer gender' with the duplicated generic sentence, and so invited the common mistake of reading a blank as a single-parent household.

value_domain: Highest school year completed, first parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1School'
variable_description: The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the adult listed first on the child's enrolment, banded into four levels. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1", so the answer comes from the enrolment form rather than from the teacher. PARENT1POSTSCHOOL holds the same adult's post-school qualification, and the two must be read together because a parent with a degree still records a school year here.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9 or equivalent or below, 88 Not known.
limitation: The scale runs backwards, so a higher code means less schooling and any model that treats the raw code as an education score inverts the result. 'Parent or carer 1' is also only the first adult on the enrolment form, so this is not the mother's education, the resident parent's education or the higher of the two.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with its instrument wording and the full four-band code list plus the 88 missing code, which is exactly what a user needs to avoid inverting the scale.
evidence_quote: What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'School level completed by first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, hiding both the reversed coding and the 88 missing convention.

value_domain: Highest school year completed, second parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2School'
variable_description: The highest year of primary or secondary school completed by the second adult on the child's enrolment, using the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2", and the column is available from the 2015 cycle onward. It is missing far more often than PARENT1SCHOOL, because it depends on the school holding details for a second adult.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Year 12 or equivalent, 2 Year 11, 3 Year 10, 4 Year 9 or equivalent or below, 88 Not known.
limitation: A gap here is not evidence of a single-parent household: the AEDC has no household composition column, so an unrecorded second adult and a genuinely absent one look identical. Taking the better-educated of the two parents also biases toward children whose enrolment happened to list two adults, since the comparison is only possible where both are present.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, the instrument wording for the second parent and the same code list as the first, which establishes that the two columns are parallel and that only presence distinguishes them.
evidence_quote: What is the highest year of primary / secondary school completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, so it neither gave the codes nor warned about the selection problem in comparing the two parents.

value_domain: Highest post-school qualification, first parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1PostSchool'
variable_description: The highest post-school qualification held by the first adult on the child's enrolment, in four broad bands from a bachelor degree down to none. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1" and records the column as available in both the Complete and Core files, while PARENT1SCHOOL is listed for the Complete file only. PARENT2POSTSCHOOL holds the same measure for the second adult.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Bachelor degree or above, 2 Advanced Diploma or Diploma, 3 Certificate level I to IV including trade qualification, 4 No post-school qualification, 88 Not known.
limitation: Code 4 is a substantive answer and 88 is the missing one, so pooling them turns parents whose qualification was not recorded into parents with none. The bands also run a Certificate I and a Certificate IV together, which covers a wide range of labour-market positions inside a single code.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with its instrument wording, its availability across file types and the full code list including the distinct 'no qualification' and 'not known' values.
evidence_quote: What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 1
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Post-school qualification of first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate code 4 from code 88, which is the mistake this column invites.

value_domain: Highest post-school qualification, second parent or carer
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2PostSchool'
variable_description: The highest post-school qualification held by the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives the collection wording as "What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2", available from the 2015 cycle in both the Complete and Core files. It is the second half of the AEDC's only measure of parental education.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 Bachelor degree or above, 2 Advanced Diploma or Diploma, 3 Certificate level I to IV including trade qualification, 4 No post-school qualification, 88 Not known.
limitation: Reducing the two parents to a household maximum needs an explicit rule for 88, which is common on the second parent and is not an education level at all. Because the column is absent whenever the school listed only one adult, a household maximum built naively is systematically higher for children with two recorded adults.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its instrument wording and the identical code list to the first-parent column, which is what makes the household-maximum construction tempting and the missing-data rule necessary.
evidence_quote: What is the highest level of post-school qualification completed by the child's parent / carer - Parent / Carer 2
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, so it neither listed the codes nor flagged the bias in combining the two parent columns.

value_domain: School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent1Occup'
variable_description: The occupation group of the first adult on the child's enrolment, in the four broad bands Australian schools collect at enrolment. The dictionary runs them from group 1, "Senior management in large business organisation, government administration and defence, and qualified professionals", down to group 4, "Machine operators, hospitality staff, assistants, labourers and related workers", with 8 for not in paid work in the last 12 months and 9 for not stated. It is pre-populated from the enrolment record rather than asked in the AEDC instrument, and it exists only from the 2021 cycle.
value_definition: A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 9. It is a broad skill-level grouping rather than an ANZSCO code, so it cannot be resolved to an occupation title or an industry.
limitation: Code 8 is not unemployment: it covers anyone not in paid work in the previous twelve months, including carers, students and retirees, and it sits outside the 1-to-4 order rather than below group 4. Because the value is copied from the enrolment form, it also describes the adult's work when the child enrolled, which can be a year or more before the assessment.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the element with the full label for each group and records the source as pre-population, which establishes both the classification and why the value is not contemporaneous with the assessment.
evidence_quote: Senior management in large business organisation, government administration and defence, and qualified professionals
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Occupation group of first parent or carer' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the groups are broad skill bands or that code 8 is not part of the ordering.

value_domain: School enrolment parental occupation group (four bands)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Parent2Occup'
variable_description: The occupation group of the second adult on the child's enrolment, on the same four bands as the first-parent column. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the occupation of the second parent or carer" and records the source as pre-population from the enrolment record, so it is not something the teacher supplied. It appears only in the 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, the shortest history of any parent column in the AEDC core file.
value_definition: A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 9, with 8 meaning not in paid work in the last 12 months and 9 not stated.
limitation: It cannot be combined with PARENT1OCCUP into a single household measure without a rule for codes 8 and 9, which are unordered and much more common on the second parent. With only two cycles it also cannot support a trend, and any 2021-to-2024 movement in the distribution may reflect how schools recorded enrolments rather than what parents do.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element and its purpose, the same code list as the first-parent column, and the 2021 introduction date, which together set both the coding and the limits of the two-cycle history.
evidence_quote: To identify the occupation of the second parent or carer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the duplicated generic sentence, so it gave no codes and no warning about combining the two parent occupation columns.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNCode' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1
variable_description: The Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, held as a code. The dictionary's file metadata gives it as "Primary Health Network code: Based on PHN_CODE 2015", so the 2015 network set is applied to every cycle, and PHNNAME on the same row is the label for the same code. It exists so AEDC results can be lined up with the areas that commission primary health services, which none of the ASGS columns match.
value_definition: Six-character text of the form PHNnnn, listed in Table 5.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables. PHN000 is 'Not available' rather than a real network.
limitation: It is the network for where the child lives, not where the child is treated and not where the school sits, and the three can differ. The assignment also comes from a concordance between SA1s and PHNs which the Department has since corrected, because "a small number of SA1s that span across multiple PHNs were re-assigned", so an older extract can carry the wrong network for those areas.
rationale: The dictionary names the classification and its vintage, the reference workbook publishes the full code and name list, and the accompanying update workbook documents the concordance error that affects the assignment.
evidence_quote: Primary Health Network code: Based on PHN_CODE 2015
supersedes_rationale: The entry lower-cased the custodian's line 'based on phn_code 2015' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the AEDC publishes the complete PHN code list in its reference tables.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNName' and Appendix 1; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.1
variable_description: The name of the Primary Health Network covering the child's home address, carried beside PHNCODE so the row reads without a lookup. The dictionary's metadata gives it as "Primary Health Network name: Based on PHN_CODE 2015", which shows the name is derived from the same 2015 code rather than assigned independently. Table 5.1 of the reference workbook holds the full code-to-name pairing.
value_definition: Text up to 44 characters taking one of the PHN names in the reference table, with 'Not available' where no network could be assigned.
limitation: A name is a weaker join key than a code. Any relabelling of a network leaves the code intact but changes the text, so matching AEDC rows to external health data on the name risks unmatched rows where PHNCODE would have matched; and neither column tells you whether the child's care actually occurs in that network.
rationale: The dictionary's Appendix 1 metadata states that the name is based on the same 2015 PHN code as PHNCODE, and the reference workbook publishes the paired list.
evidence_quote: Primary Health Network name: Based on PHN_CODE 2015
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the lower-cased custodian phrase with the generic sentence printed twice, and did not say that the name is only a label for PHNCODE.

value_domain: AEDC reportability indicator for a Primary Health Network
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHNPublic'
variable_description: Says whether AEDC results for the child's Primary Health Network may be published, and names the reason when they may not. The dictionary lists 1 for "PHN has AEDC results publicly available" and then five suppression reasons: fewer than 80 per cent of all non-special-needs children, location not available, fewer than 15 valid AEDC children, fewer than two teachers, and the last two together. It is an attribute of the network repeated on every child in it, so it constrains reporting rather than describing the child.
value_definition: An integer taking 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 or 23, where 1 is publishable and the rest are named suppression reasons.
limitation: It restricts publication, not analysis, and it is not a quality flag for the child: a child in a suppressed network has the same valid domain scores as anyone else. Because the indicator is computed on whichever network the child was assigned to, the corrected SA1-to-PHN concordance the Department later issued can move both the assignment and the publishability of small networks.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the full code list with each suppression reason spelled out, and the accompanying update workbook documents the concordance correction that feeds the assignment.
evidence_quote: PHN not public: Less than 15 AEDC children valid
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Phn reportability indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the AEDC publishes the six codes and what each one means.

value_domain: AEDC physical health and wellbeing domain score (0 to 10)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYS' and section 3.1
variable_description: The child's score on the physical health and wellbeing domain, built from the teacher's answers about gross and fine motor skills, physical independence and readiness for the school day. The dictionary defines the element as "Physical health and wellbeing", records it as derived, and states that for each domain children receive "a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development". PHYSCATEGORY turns this score into a percentile band and PHYSVALID says whether it should be used at all.
value_definition: A number between 0 and 10 held to four decimal places, calculated only where at least 75 per cent of the domain's instrument items were completed. The calculation itself is licensed from the Offord Centre at McMaster University and is not published.
limitation: It is not a diagnosis and was not built for the individual child: the dictionary warns that the AEDC indicators "have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children" and were validated as population measures. A raw score also cannot be compared across domains, since each domain has its own distribution and its own cut-offs, so a 7 here and a 7 on social competence are not the same standing.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its format and its derived status, and section 3.1 sets out the 0-to-10 scale, the 75 per cent completion rule and the population-level caveat.
evidence_quote: For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only 'Physical health and wellbeing' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never gave the scale, the completion rule or the warning against individual-level use.

value_domain: AEDC domain percentile band, physical health and wellbeing
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYSCategory' and section 3.1
variable_description: Which band of the 2009 national distribution the child's physical health and wellbeing score falls into: 1 is "0 to 10th percentile", 2 is "11th to 25th percentile", 3 is the 26th to 50th and 4 the 51st to 100th. This is the column that produces the AEDC's headline language, since band 1 is developmentally vulnerable and band 2 developmentally at risk, and LOWTOTAL counts how many of the five domains sit at 1. The cut-offs were set on the 2009 population and have not moved since.
value_definition: A single-digit integer taking 1, 2, 3 or 4, defined by fixed percentile cut-offs applied to PHYS. The dictionary notes the categories are not calculated for children with diagnosed special needs or aged under four.
limitation: It is not a quartile of the current cohort, so a rising share in band 4 means children doing better than 2009 children rather than better than their peers. The bands are also unequal in width - 10, 15, 25 and 50 percentage points - so treating the codes as an evenly spaced scale misreads the distribution.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the four percentile bands verbatim and section 3.1 states that the cut-offs come from the 2009 baseline and are held constant across cycles.
evidence_quote: The cut off percentile for each domain category are based on the baseline set in the 2009 AEDC data collection.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Vulnerable - physical health and wellbeing' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which both hid the four-band coding and implied the column is a vulnerability flag rather than a percentile band.

value_domain: Domain validity flag, physical health and wellbeing (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PHYSValid'
variable_description: Says whether the child's physical health and wellbeing score should be used at all. The dictionary defines 1 as a child who "does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", and 0 as failing any one of those tests. It is the filter to apply before analysing PHYS or PHYSCATEGORY, and each of the five domains has its own version, so a child can be valid on one domain and not another.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for valid and 0 for not valid. VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of the five are 1 for the child and TOTALMISS counts the scales that could not be built.
limitation: A zero does not say which of the three exclusions applied, so special needs status, being three years old and too many unanswered items are indistinguishable here and SPECIALNEEDS and the age columns are needed to separate them. It is also not a flag for an unreliable score: a domain can be valid while resting on only the minimum share of completed items.
rationale: The dictionary publishes both code labels in full, which name the three exclusion tests the flag combines and show why a zero is ambiguous.
evidence_quote: Child has special needs status, is 3 years old or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Valid - physical health and wellbeing' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither gave the two codes nor named the exclusions behind them.

value_domain: Preschool or kindergarten attendance in the year before school (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'Preschool'
variable_description: Whether the teacher reported the child as having attended a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before school started. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying a child "reported as attending a pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school" and notes it is only answered where instrument item E2 was answered yes, so it depends on the teacher knowing the child's history. PSDC is the broader column that also counts day care, and DAYCARENO is day care without a preschool program.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 1 for yes and 0 for no. Unlike PSDC and DAYCARENO it carries no 88 'Don't know' code, so uncertainty resolves to 0.
limitation: It is a teacher's report rather than an enrolment record, so attendance the teacher did not know about is counted as none, and it says nothing about dose - hours, months and continuity are not captured anywhere in the AEDC. The dictionary also records a derivation revision in 2018, so a change in the rate between 2015 and 2018 can be a change in the rule rather than in behaviour.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its purpose, the E2 filter, the two permitted values and the 2018 derivation revision, which together explain both what the column counts and where a break in series sits.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was reported as attending a pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Attended a pre-school program' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say the value is a teacher report, that it lacks a 'don't know' code, or that the derivation changed in 2018.

value_domain: Day care or preschool attendance in the year before school (yes/no)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'PSDC'
