variable_description: Whether the child was reported as attending either a day care centre or a preschool or kindergarten program in the year before starting school - the widest of the AEDC's three early-childhood attendance columns. The dictionary gives its purpose as identifying a child "reported as attending a day care centre or pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school", so it is the union of PRESCHOOL and DAYCARENO rather than a separate question. Like them it is only answered where instrument item E2 was answered yes.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 yes, 0 no, 88 'Don't know', which is the AEDC's standard missing-data convention.
limitation: Because it merges formal preschool with day care it cannot support any claim about preschool specifically; that distinction lives in PRESCHOOL and DAYCARENO. The 88 code is also stored as a number, so leaving it in an average silently treats 'don't know' as a very large value rather than as missing.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element, its purpose, the E2 filter and the three permitted values including the 88 convention documented in section 5.2.
evidence_quote: To identify if this child was reported as attending a day care centre or pre-school or kindergarten program in the year before starting school.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Attended day care or pre-school program' with the duplicated generic sentence, and so failed to warn that an 88 in a numeric column will silently corrupt an average.

value_domain: AEDC reportability indicator for a Regional Development Australia area
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'RDAPublic'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 5.2
variable_description: Says whether AEDC results for the child's Regional Development Australia area may be published, and names the reason when they may not. The dictionary lists 1 for "RDA has AEDC results publicly available" alongside suppression codes for fewer than 80 per cent of non-special-needs children, location not available, fewer than 15 valid AEDC children, fewer than two teachers, and the last two combined. RDACODE and RDANAME on the same row identify the area it refers to, and Table 5.2 of the reference workbook lists them.
value_definition: An integer taking 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 or 23, using the same suppression scheme as the SA2, SA3, LGA and PHN publishability columns.
limitation: It says nothing about the child's own data quality and nothing about whether the smaller areas the child sits in can be published: an RDA can be reportable while its component SA2s are suppressed. RDA areas are also committee footprints rather than statistical areas, so this column cannot stand in for a geographic suppression rule on the ASGS columns.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the six codes with their suppression reasons spelled out, and the reference workbook publishes the RDA code and name list the indicator attaches to.
evidence_quote: RDA not public: Less than two teachers
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Rda region reportability indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the AEDC publishes all six codes and their meanings.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entries 'RegionID' and 'Region'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1
variable_description: The code for the AEDC Region the child lives in, which is the AEDC's own reporting geography rather than an ABS one. The dictionary defines the companion column as "The AEDC Region where the child lives", and Table 2.1 of the reference workbook shows the hierarchy this code sits inside: LocalCommunityID within CommunityID within RegionID within StateID. The AEDC publishes results at Local Community, Community, state and national level, and this code identifies the tier those communities are grouped into; no ASGS column reproduces the hierarchy.
value_definition: A three-digit integer keyed to Table 2.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where each region carries a name and a state; REGION on the same row is the label.
limitation: The boundaries are not fixed history. The community geography this code sits above was rebuilt for the 2024 collection and "applied retrospectively to all previous collections", so a region's 2009 figures in this file need not match what the AEDC published in 2009. Regions are also built from SA1 blocks for comparability with ABS data rather than to match any administrative boundary, so they are not LGAs, PHNs or RDAs.
rationale: The dictionary defines the AEDC Region and documents the retrospective boundary revision, and the reference workbook publishes the full local community, community, region and state hierarchy against this code.
evidence_quote: Revised Local Community and Community boundaries were used for the 2024 and applied retrospectively to all previous collections to allow trend analysis over all six cycles.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Region identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it neither named the AEDC's own geography hierarchy nor warned that the boundaries were rebuilt and backdated.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'Remoteness'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.3
variable_description: The name of the ABS remoteness class for the child's home address - Major Cities, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote or Very Remote. The dictionary's file metadata gives it as "Remoteness area name: Based on RA_NAME_2021", so it is the label of REMOTENESSCODE on the same row rather than a separate classification. Unlike the code it carries no state digit, so grouping on it gives the five national classes directly.
value_definition: Text up to 38 characters taking one of the five ASGS 2021 Remoteness Area names or 'Not available', as listed in Table 3.3 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables.
limitation: It describes where the child lives, not the journey to school or the school's own remoteness, which differ in border areas and wherever children travel to a regional centre. Because the 2021 boundaries are applied to all six cycles, a community that became less remote over time will show the same class in every cycle.
rationale: The dictionary's Appendix 1 names the exact ABS field the column is based on, and the reference workbook publishes the code-to-name list including the 'Not available' entry.
evidence_quote: Remoteness area name: Based on RA_NAME_2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the lower-cased custodian phrase with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, despite the AEDC publishing the complete five-class list in its reference tables.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'RemotenessCode'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.3
variable_description: The ABS remoteness class of the child's home address, held as a two-digit code whose first digit is the state. The dictionary's metadata gives it as "Remoteness area code: Based on RA_CODE_2021", and Table 3.3 of the reference workbook shows the pattern: 10 to 14 run Major Cities through Very Remote in New South Wales, 20 to 24 do the same in Victoria, and so on. REMOTENESS is the plain name for the same classification.
value_definition: A two-digit integer, state digit followed by remoteness class, with 0 meaning 'Not available'. The classes are the five ASGS 2021 Remoteness Areas: Major Cities, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote.
limitation: Grouping on the code directly produces state-by-remoteness cells rather than the five national classes, because the state is baked into the leading digit; only the second digit is the remoteness class. The classification also measures road distance to service centres, so it is a measure of access rather than of population density or disadvantage - SEIFASCORE is the disadvantage column.
rationale: The reference workbook's remoteness table shows the state-prefixed code structure directly, and the dictionary's Appendix 1 names the ABS field it derives from.
evidence_quote: Remoteness area code: Based on RA_CODE_2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Remoteness area code' with the duplicated generic sentence, hiding the published code list and, more importantly, that the code is state-specific and cannot be grouped as a national class.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'SA2Code'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.1
variable_description: The ABS Statistical Area Level 2 in which the child lives, coded on the 2021 boundaries. The dictionary's file metadata gives it as "Statistical area level 2 code: Based on SA2_9DIGITCODE_2021", so one fixed geography is applied to every cycle back to 2009 and areas stay comparable over time. SA2NAME is its label and SA2PUBLIC says whether results for it may be published.
value_definition: The ASGS 2021 SA2 code, published with its SA1, SA3, SA4, GCCSA and state in Table 3.1 of the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where it is listed in nine-digit form; the dictionary's own field format for the column says five digits, so check the width before joining. A value of 0 means the location was not available.
limitation: It is where the child lives, not where the school is; SCHOOLSTATE and SCHOOLSUBURB describe the school and can fall in a different area entirely. Because the 2021 boundaries are applied retrospectively, an SA2 total for the 2009 cycle will not match the figures the AEDC published in 2009 on the boundaries of the day.
rationale: The dictionary's Appendix 1 names the exact ABS field, and the reference workbook publishes the full SA1-to-state hierarchy showing the nine-digit form the column takes.
evidence_quote: Statistical area level 2 code: Based on SA2_9DIGITCODE_2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the lower-cased custodian phrase with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not say which ASGS edition applies or that the coding is applied backwards over earlier cycles.

value_domain: AEDC reportability indicator for an SA2
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'SA2Public'; AEDC Update to PHN and LGAPublic, SA2Public and SA3Public variables
variable_description: Says whether AEDC results for the child's Statistical Area Level 2 may be published, and names the reason when they may not. The dictionary lists 1 for "SA2 has AEDC results publicly available" and suppression codes 5, 9, 21, 22 and 23 covering low coverage of non-special-needs children, missing location, fewer than 15 valid children, fewer than two teachers, and both together. It qualifies the SA2CODE and SA2NAME on the row, not the child.
value_definition: An integer taking 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 or 23; the identical scheme is used for SA3PUBLIC, LGAPUBLIC, PHNPUBLIC and RDAPUBLIC.
limitation: For the first cycle the indicator is calculated on a base that includes the 2010 collection, which the AEDC otherwise excludes above Local Community level; the Department publishes a reissued SA2Public by year for that reason and notes that "only the reportability indicator for 2009/2010 should change". A 2009 suppression read straight from this column can therefore be wrong.
rationale: The dictionary publishes all six codes with their reasons, and the Department's companion workbook documents the 2010 problem in the Cycle 1 values and supplies the corrected series.
evidence_quote: The current reportability indicator in the AEDC microdata is based on Cycle which includes 2010 data by default for Cycle 1.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'SA2 publishable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, giving neither the codes nor the known defect in the first cycle's values.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'SA3Code'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.1
variable_description: The ABS Statistical Area Level 3 containing the child's home address, on the 2021 boundaries. The dictionary's metadata gives it as "Statistical area level 3 code: Based on SA3_CODE_2021", and it is a strict aggregation of the SA2 on the same row rather than an independently assigned area. It is the level at which many AEDC results survive the publishability tests that suppress smaller areas.
value_definition: A five-digit ASGS 2021 SA3 code whose leading digit is the state; it nests inside the SA4 on the same row. Table 3.1 of the reference workbook holds the full hierarchy.
limitation: Averaging child-level results to SA3 is not the same as averaging published SA2 results, because children in suppressed SA2s still count towards the SA3 total. It also cannot stand in for a service catchment: SA3s are ABS statistical areas, and PHNCODE and RDACODE are the columns tied to administrative regions.
rationale: The dictionary's Appendix 1 names the ABS field, and the reference workbook publishes the SA2-SA3-SA4 nesting that makes the aggregation exact.
evidence_quote: Statistical area level 3 code: Based on SA3_CODE_2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the lower-cased custodian phrase with the duplicated generic sentence, and so did not name the ASGS edition or explain how the level relates to SA2 suppression.

value_domain: AEDC reportability indicator for an SA3
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'SA3Public'; AEDC Update to PHN and LGAPublic, SA2Public and SA3Public variables
variable_description: Says whether AEDC results for the child's Statistical Area Level 3 may be published, and names the reason when they may not. The dictionary lists 1 for "SA3 has AEDC results publicly available" and the same five suppression codes used at SA2 and LGA level: low coverage of non-special-needs children, missing location, fewer than 15 valid children, fewer than two teachers, and both. It describes the area, so every child in the SA3 carries the same value.
value_definition: An integer taking 1, 5, 9, 21, 22 or 23, matching the scheme on SA2PUBLIC, LGAPUBLIC, PHNPUBLIC and RDAPUBLIC.
limitation: Publishability at SA3 does not imply publishability at SA2. An SA3 can pass the 15-child and two-teacher tests on the strength of one large SA2 inside it while several of its other SA2s are suppressed, so filtering on this column does not yield a set of publishable SA2 results. Like SA2PUBLIC, the Cycle 1 value is computed on a base that includes the 2010 collection.
rationale: The dictionary publishes the code list with each reason, and the Department's companion workbook supplies a corrected SA3Public by year, confirming both the scheme and the first-cycle defect.
evidence_quote: SA3 not public: Less than 15 AEDC children valid and less than two teachers
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'SA3 publishable' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it neither gave the codes nor warned that publishability does not cascade down to SA2.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, Appendix 1 entry 'SA4Code'; AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 3.1
variable_description: The ABS Statistical Area Level 4 containing the child's home address, the coarsest ASGS unit below the state in the AEDC core file. The dictionary's metadata gives it as "Statistical area level 4 code: Based on SA4_CODE_2021", and it nests the SA3 and SA2 codes on the same row. SA4NAME is its label.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS 2021 SA4 code whose leading digit is the state identifier, published with its SA2, SA3 and GCCSA in Table 3.1 of the reference workbook.
limitation: There is no SA4PUBLIC column, so the absence of a suppression flag at this level is not a licence to publish - judgement has to come from the smaller areas or from the AEDC's own community geography. SA4s also hold populations in the hundreds of thousands, so a stable rate here can conceal exactly the local variation the AEDC exists to show.
rationale: The dictionary's Appendix 1 names the ABS field and lists which levels carry a publishability column, and the reference workbook shows the SA4 code structure and its nesting.
evidence_quote: Statistical area level 4 code: Based on SA4_CODE_2021
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the lower-cased custodian phrase with the duplicated generic sentence, and did not note that SA4 is the one geography level in the file without a reportability indicator.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'SchoolAGEID'
variable_description: The Australian Government's own code for the school the child attended, rather than an identifier minted for the AEDC. The dictionary defines it as "The individual school code used by the Australian Government to identify each school participating in the AEDC", renamed from AGSchoolID in 2024 and from DSchoolID in 2018; the PLIDA metadata still carries the older DEEWR wording. It is the column to use when joining AEDC schools to other Commonwealth school collections; SCHOOLID is the internal AEDC key.
value_definition: A five-digit integer allocated by the Australian Government, distinct from the eight-digit AEDC SCHOOLID on the same row.
limitation: A blank is not an absent school. The dictionary records the field as "Suppressed for schools outside of a data recipient's jurisdiction", so counting distinct values undercounts schools in any extract spanning more than one state, and the pattern of missingness follows the data-sharing agreement rather than the schools.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element definition, the five-digit format, the two renames and the suppression rule, which together explain both what the identifier is and why it goes missing.
evidence_quote: Suppressed for schools outside of a data recipient's jurisdiction.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'National school identifier used by deewr' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not explain the DEEWR naming, the difference from SCHOOLID, or the jurisdictional suppression.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (February 2025), Department of Education, entry 'SchoolID'
variable_description: The de-identified code for the school the child attended when the instrument was completed, and the column that ties a child's row together across the five AEDC tables in a cycle. The dictionary defines it as a code that distinguishes each participating school "without providing any identifying information", so it is an arbitrary key rather than a national school number - SCHOOLAGEID is the Australian Government identifier. SCHOOLTYPE, SCHOOLSTATE and SCHOOLSUBURB describe the same school on the same row.
value_definition: An eight-digit integer with no internal meaning; the digits do not encode state, sector or region, and the code cannot be decoded back to a named school.
limitation: It identifies a school, not a place of residence: the geography columns on the same row are coded from where the child lives, so grouping by SCHOOLID and grouping by SA2CODE answer different questions. It also does not identify the class or the teacher, which is what TEACHERID and the CLASSTYPE columns are for.
rationale: The dictionary gives the element definition, its de-identified purpose and its eight-digit format, and the PLIDA tables show it on every one of the thirty AEDC tables, which is what makes it the within-cycle join key.
evidence_quote: The School ID uses a unique numerical code to distinguish each school participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'School identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it did not distinguish the AEDC's internal key from the Australian Government school code or say that the value carries no structure.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SchoolState
variable_description: The state or territory of the school whose teacher completed the instrument for this child, assigned on the school's location. The dictionary puts it as "A school is assigned to a state or territory based on geographic location", which makes it a property of the school rather than of the child: STATE on the same row is where the child lives, and the dictionary notes that "most published AEDC information uses the variable State (state in which child resides) not SchoolState". It sits with SCHOOLID, SCHOOLTYPE and TEACHERID as the school-side block of the core table, and it is one of the few school fields released on the linkage version of the file.
value_definition: Three characters of left-justified text drawn from a closed list of eight: ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA. No code for overseas or unknown is published.
limitation: It is not the child's state of residence, so a border-town record can carry one jurisdiction here and another in STATE, and a jurisdictional count built on this column counts schools' children rather than residents' children. It is also not fixed history: when responsibility for a school moved between jurisdictions in the 2021 collection, the dictionary records that SchoolState was updated across all cycles while the published national reports kept the old figures, so this column and an old report can disagree by design.
rationale: The dictionary's SchoolState entry gives the definition, the three-character format and the full eight-value list, and its appendix A2.1.2 records the retrospective jurisdiction change and warns that published AEDC reporting uses State instead.
evidence_quote: A school is assigned to a state or territory based on geographic location.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'School state' with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both value definition and limitation, so it neither gave the eight abbreviations nor warned that this is the school's jurisdiction rather than the child's.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SchoolType
variable_description: The sector of the school the child was attending in their first year of full-time school, as governance rather than as funding. The dictionary defines it as "Each school in Australia is classified as Government, Independent or Catholic, depending on the type of governance they operate under", the standard three-sector split used across Australian schooling statistics. Because AEDC participation is close to a census of that year level, the distribution of this column is a rough picture of where five-year-olds start school, and it is the field used with SEIFACATEGORY and REMOTENESS to describe the schooling context a child's domain scores were reported in.
value_definition: One character of left-justified text: C for Catholic, G for Government and I for Independent.
limitation: Sector is not fee level, religious character or funding mix. A low-fee Christian school and a high-fee non-denominational school are both I, and nothing here separates a mainstream government school from a government school for specific purposes. It also describes the school, not the child's earlier care, which PRESCHOOL, DAYCARE and PSDC carry.
rationale: The dictionary's SchoolType entry gives the governance definition, the purpose statement naming the three sectors, and the complete one-character code frame.
evidence_quote: Each school in Australia is classified as Government, Independent or Catholic, depending on the type of governance they operate under.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's 'School type' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the field holds a single letter from a three-value sector classification.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD quintile, national, at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFACategory
variable_description: The national disadvantage quintile of the small area the child lives in, which the dictionary states as "SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia". The underlying measure is the ABS Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage computed from Census data for the child's Statistical Area Level 1, so it describes the neighbourhood and not the household. It is the socio-economic field carried in every AEDC cycle table here, where SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE appear only from the 2018 file onward, and it is distinct from LCABSSEIFACATEGORY, which reports SEIFA for the much larger AEDC local community, built by population-weighted averaging of the component area scores.
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 1 to 5, where 1 is quintile 1 (most disadvantaged) and 5 is quintile 5 (least disadvantaged); the dictionary declares the field as an eight-length integer.
limitation: A quintile of an area is not a measure of a family, and many children in the most advantaged quintile live in poor households, so reading category 1 as 'this child is disadvantaged' is the ecological fallacy the ABS warns against. The quintiles are also cut nationally, so a state where few areas fall in quintile 1 has fewer children in that category by geography rather than by need, and the cut points move between SEIFA releases rather than between cycles: the dictionary records the 2011 SEIFA behind the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycles, the 2016 SEIFA behind 2018, and the 2021 SEIFA behind both 2021 and 2024.
rationale: The dictionary's SEIFACategory entry gives the purpose statement naming IRSD quintiles within Australia and prints all five labelled values, and the ABS SEIFA release defines IRSD itself.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD category (quintile) within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'SEIFA category' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it named neither the index, nor the direction of the scale, nor the geography it is measured on.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD decile, national, at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFADecile
variable_description: The national disadvantage decile of the small area the child lives in, given by the dictionary as "SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia", and a finer cut of the ranking SEIFACATEGORY holds in quintiles. The ABS builds it by ordering every Statistical Area Level 1 by its IRSD score and splitting the ordered list into ten equal groups, so the value is a position in the national distribution rather than a quantity. In this registry it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables, alongside SEIFAPERCENTILE and SEIFARANK, which is why an analysis spanning all six cycles has to fall back on SEIFACATEGORY.
value_definition: A two-digit integer from 1 to 10. The ABS assigns it by rank: "All areas are ordered from lowest to highest score, the lowest 10% of areas are given a decile number of one...up to the highest 10% of areas which are given a decile number of 10", so 1 is the most disadvantaged tenth.
limitation: Deciles are ranks, so the gap between decile 1 and decile 2 is not the same amount of disadvantage as the gap between decile 5 and decile 6, and averaging them produces a number with no interpretation. The decile also comes from the SEIFA release the dictionary assigns to the cycle, the 2016 SEIFA for 2018 and the 2021 SEIFA for both 2021 and 2024, so an area that keeps the same decile across cycles has kept its position relative to other areas rather than its circumstances.
rationale: The dictionary defines the field as the national IRSD decile and gives its two-digit integer format, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper defines how deciles are formed from ranked SA1 scores.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD decile within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Seifa - irsd decile within australia' as its whole description with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said that the values run 1 to 10 with 1 most disadvantaged, nor that the column is missing from half the AEDC cycles in this asset.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAExcluded
variable_description: A marker that the child's small area has no SEIFA score to report, which the dictionary describes as denoting "SEIFA – Denotes unavailability of SEIFA data in particular statistical areas". It exists because the ABS does not score every Statistical Area Level 1: published exclusion rules drop areas with no or very small populations, with very few employed people or classifiable private dwellings, and with most people counted in non-private dwellings, and those areas are left without an index value. Read it before using SEIFASCORE, SEIFACATEGORY, SEIFADECILE or SEIFAPERCENTILE, since it is the column that tells you an empty or implausible value there is a deliberate absence rather than a data fault.
value_definition: A single character of left-justified text. The dictionary declares the format but publishes no code list, so the specific letter or letters used to mark exclusion are not documented.
limitation: It does not say which exclusion rule applied, and the rules differ in what they imply: a tiny population is a statistical limit, while an area where most people live in non-private dwellings is a coverage problem that may itself correlate with disadvantage. Excluded areas are also not spread evenly across the country, so dropping these children removes a clustered group rather than a random slice.
rationale: The dictionary's SEIFAExcluded entry gives the purpose and the one-character text format but no values, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper supplies what exclusion means: some SA1s receive no index score under published exclusion rules.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – Denotes unavailability of SEIFA data in particular statistical areas.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'SEIFA excluded flag' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which left the reader unable to tell whether the flag concerned the child, the school or the area, or what an exclusion implies for the other SEIFA columns.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD percentile, national, at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAPercentile
variable_description: The child's small area placed in the national disadvantage ranking to the nearest hundredth, described by the dictionary as "SEIFA – IRSD percentile within Australia". It is the finest of the three ranked SEIFA columns in the AEDC file, with SEIFADECILE grouping the same ordering into tenths and SEIFACATEGORY into fifths, and it is the one to use when a study needs a continuous area-disadvantage control without depending on the score's scale. Like the decile, it appears only in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables here.
value_definition: A three-digit integer from 1 to 100. The ABS forms it by ordering all areas by score, so "the lowest 1% of areas are given a percentile number of one...up to the highest 1% of areas which are given a percentile number of 100".
limitation: Because it is a rank, an area can shift many percentiles between cycles without its own circumstances changing, purely because other areas moved. It also cannot be compared with the percentile of a different SEIFA index or a different geography: a percentile computed over SA1s is not the same yardstick as one computed over suburbs or local government areas.
rationale: The dictionary names the field as the national IRSD percentile and gives the three-digit integer format, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper defines how percentiles are assigned from ranked SA1 scores.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD percentile within Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's line 'Seifa - irsd percentile within australia' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, giving no range, no direction and no relationship to the decile and category columns beside it.

value_domain: SEIFA IRSD index score at SA1
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SEIFAScore
variable_description: The underlying disadvantage index value for the child's neighbourhood, which the dictionary defines as the "SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives". The ABS builds the Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage from Census variables such as low income, low educational attainment, unemployment and crowded dwellings, then rescales the result, so a lower score means more disadvantage. In this asset the column is present in the 2009, 2012 and 2015 cycle tables only; the later cycles carry the ranked forms in SEIFARANK, SEIFADECILE and SEIFAPERCENTILE instead.
value_definition: A numeric field declared as 12.8, so up to eight decimal places. The ABS standardises index scores across all scored areas: "We then rescale the raw scores to a mean of 1,000 and standard deviation of 100 to create a new set of scores that are the index scores in SEIFA."
limitation: The scale is set within each SEIFA release, so a score of 950 in the 2011-based index and 950 in the 2016-based index describe a similar position among areas of their day, not the same living conditions. The three cycles that carry this column all draw on the 2011 SEIFA, so a difference in score between them reflects a different area rather than a change in an area's circumstances. The index also summarises disadvantage only, so a high score is an absence of measured disadvantage rather than evidence of advantage, which is a separate ABS index.
rationale: The dictionary's SEIFAScore entry names the index, the geography and the numeric format, and the ABS SEIFA technical paper gives the standardisation that fixes what the number means.
evidence_quote: SEIFA – IRSD score based on the SA1 in which the child lives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'SEIFA score' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it gave no scale, no direction, no geography, and no warning that the column stops after the 2015 cycle in this asset.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOC and section 3.1 Domain Indicators
variable_description: The child's social competence score, one of the five AEDC domain scores a teacher's instrument responses are reduced to. The dictionary states that "AEDC domain scores are calculated based on teacher responses to the relevant domain questions for each child", and for this domain the questions are the twenty-four C-series items C1 to C23 and C25, covering overall social competence, responsibility and respect, approaches to learning, and readiness to explore new things; the sub-domain scores SOC_1 to SOC_4 report those four strands separately. Two columns qualify it on the same row: SOCVALID says whether the score should be used at all, and SOCCATEGORY places it in the percentile band that turns it into the published vulnerable, at-risk and on-track categories.
value_definition: A numeric field declared as 7.4, so four decimal places. The dictionary states that "For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development", and the score is only computed where 75 per cent or more of the domain's items were completed.
limitation: It cannot be recomputed or audited from the item responses in the same file, because the domain score methodology is licensed from the Offord Centre for Child Studies and is not published. It is also not a diagnostic reading of one child: the dictionary states the indicators "have not been psychometrically tested for application in relation to individual children" and were validated as a population measure at group level, so a single child's score should not be used to say anything about that child.
rationale: The dictionary gives the SOC entry, the 0 to 10 domain scale, the 75 per cent item completion rule, the table allocating C-series items to the social competence domain, and the statements about licensing and group-level validity.
evidence_quote: For each of the five AEDC domains, children receive a score between zero and ten, where higher scores denote higher levels of development.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Social competence' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it gave no range, no direction, no completion rule and no warning against individual-level use.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCCategory
variable_description: Where the child's social competence score sits against the fixed 2009 national cut-offs, banded into four percentile ranges. The dictionary gives its purpose as "To identify the grouping variable for the cumulative frequency of scores in the social competence domain", and it is the column that produces published AEDC reporting: band 1 is developmentally vulnerable on this domain, band 2 is developmentally at risk, and bands 3 and 4 are on track. It also feeds the summary indicators, since DV1 and DV2 count how many of the five domain categories fall in band 1.
value_definition: A single-digit integer with four values: 1 for the 0 to 10th percentile, 2 for the 11th to 25th, 3 for the 26th to 50th and 4 for the 51st to 100th. The percentiles are the cut-off scores set in the 2009 collection and held constant since.
limitation: The bands are not recomputed each cycle, so they do not divide the current cohort into fixed shares: finding more or fewer than 10 per cent of children in band 1 in 2021 is the result rather than an error. The column is also not calculated for every child, since categories are only produced where the domain score is valid, which excludes children with special needs status and children aged three.
rationale: The dictionary's SOCCategory entry publishes the four percentile bands in full, and its section 3.1 records that the cut-offs come from the 2009 baseline and have been held constant to keep later cycles comparable.
evidence_quote: To identify the grouping variable for the cumulative frequency of scores in the social competence domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Vulnerable - social competence' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, implying a yes-or-no vulnerability flag when the column actually holds a four-band percentile grouping in which only band 1 means vulnerable.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry SOCValid
variable_description: Whether this child's social competence result may be used, which the dictionary states as being "To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain". It is the gate on SOC and SOCCATEGORY: a child can carry a stored score while this column says the score does not qualify for reporting. Each of the five domains has its own flag of this shape, and VALIDDOMAINS counts how many of them are set to 1 for the child.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 1 where the child "does not have special needs, is not 3 years old and has minimum number of valid instrument responses for the domain", and 0 where the child has special needs status, is three years old, or has too many unanswered instrument questions for the domain.
limitation: A 0 does not tell you which of its three causes applied, so it cannot be used as a measure of item non-response; SPECIALNEEDS and the age fields have to be checked to separate a child excluded by rule from one whose teacher left questions blank. It is also a statement about this domain only, not about the instrument as a whole, which is what VALIDINSTRUMENT covers.
rationale: The dictionary's SOCValid entry gives the purpose statement and both labelled values, including the three conditions that force a zero.
evidence_quote: To identify the validity of the child's results on the social competence domain.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Valid - social competence' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never revealed that invalidity mixes an administrative exclusion with genuine missing responses.

value_source: AEDC Data Guidelines (Australian Government Department of Education, 2025), glossary entry Special needs, with the code frame in the AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 entry SpecialNeeds
variable_description: Whether the teacher recorded the child as having special needs status when completing the instrument. The Data Guidelines define the term as applying to "children reported by teachers as requiring special assistance because of chronic medical, physical, or intellectually disabling conditions (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome) based on a medical diagnosis or diagnoses". The value governs most of the rest of the record: children flagged 1 are counted in the AEDC population, but their domain results are ruled invalid and their domain categories are not calculated, which is why the published denominators, and the 80 per cent coverage rule that VALIDINSTRUMENT serves, count only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0.
value_definition: A single-digit integer: 0 for not special needs and 1 for special needs. The item is asked of the teacher as "Is this child considered Special Needs".
limitation: It is the teacher's report at the time of the collection, made against a medical diagnosis but recorded through school processes, so the share flagged is not a prevalence estimate for disability and should not be compared between jurisdictions without care. It also says nothing about the condition itself, which the D-series items on the AEDC special needs table carry.
rationale: The AEDC Data Guidelines glossary defines special needs status and sets out its role in the coverage rule denominator, and the Data Dictionary publishes the two-value code frame and the instrument wording.
evidence_quote: Term applying to children reported by teachers as requiring special assistance because of chronic medical, physical, or intellectually disabling conditions (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome) based on a medical diagnosis or diagnoses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's 'Special needs status' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, hiding the fact that this one flag suppresses every domain score and category on the row.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry State
variable_description: The state or territory the child lives in, given by the dictionary as "The state or territory in which the child resides" and derived rather than reported directly by the teacher. It is the jurisdiction field AEDC reporting actually uses, and the dictionary says so explicitly: most published AEDC information uses this column and not SCHOOLSTATE. STATEID on the same row is the numeric form of the same fact, and the geography chain below it runs through REGION, LOCALCOMMUNITY, LGA and the ABS statistical areas.
value_definition: Three characters of left-justified text from the same closed eight-value list as SCHOOLSTATE: ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA.
limitation: Because it is derived from the child's recorded address at the time of the collection, it is a point-in-time residence and not a history: a child who moved interstate between school enrolment and the instrument is placed where they were when the record was built. It is also not the jurisdiction responsible for the child's schooling, which is SCHOOLSTATE and can differ near borders.
rationale: The dictionary's State entry gives the residence definition, marks the field as derived, prints the eight abbreviations, and its appendix records that published AEDC information uses State rather than SchoolState.
evidence_quote: The state or territory in which the child resides.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'State or territory' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say whose state this is, that the field is derived, or that it is the jurisdiction AEDC publications use.

value_domain: AEDC state electoral division publication reason code
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateElectoratePublic
variable_description: Whether AEDC results may be published for the state electoral division the child lives in, and if not, which rule stopped them. The dictionary describes the field as the "SED reportability indicator" and prints six codes, one meaning publishable and five naming a specific failure: too few valid children, too few teachers, both, coverage below 80 per cent of non-special-needs children, or no location. It is the electorate member of a family of publication codes that also covers communities (CPUBLIC), local communities (LCPUBLIC), Indigenous areas (IAREPUBLIC) and statistical areas, and it appears in the 2018, 2021 and 2024 cycle tables only.
value_definition: A single-digit stored value drawn from six codes: 1 publicly available; 5 less than 80 per cent of all non-special-needs children; 9 location not available; 21 fewer than 15 valid AEDC children; 22 fewer than two teachers; 23 both fewer than 15 valid children and fewer than two teachers.
limitation: It is a rule about reporting an area, not a judgement on the child: a code of 21 or 22 does not mean this row is unreliable, only that the electorate it belongs to is too thin to report. It also carries nothing about which electoral boundaries applied, so it cannot be used to align a cycle's results with a particular redistribution; STATEELECTORATECODE and STATEELECTORATE hold the identity of the division.
rationale: The dictionary's StateElectoratePublic entry publishes all six reportability codes with their labels and gives the one-digit integer format, matching the pattern documented for the other AEDC publication indicators.
evidence_quote: State Electorate not public: Less than 15 AEDC children valid and less than two teachers
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviation 'Sed reportability indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it neither expanded SED nor showed that the field holds a published six-value reason code.

value_domain: AEDC state and territory code (1 to 8)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry StateID, with the codes in the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, Table 2.1 AEDC Geography
variable_description: The numeric code for the state or territory the child lives in, which the dictionary states as a "Code for state in which child resides". It is the join key at the top of the AEDC's own geography hierarchy, which runs state, region, community and local community, so it pairs with REGIONID, COMMUNITYID and LOCALCOMMUNITYID rather than with any ABS geography code. STATE on the same row carries the same fact as a three-letter abbreviation, and the reference tables that publish the code list are also what expands REGIONID and LOCALCOMMUNITYID.
value_definition: A single-digit integer running 1 to 8 in the ABS jurisdiction order: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory. The dictionary defers the list to the AEDC Data Dictionary Reference Tables, where Table 2.1 carries it against every AEDC local community.
limitation: It is not an ABS state code in the sense of the ASGS state and territory structure, which carries a further code for Other Territories: the dictionary records that the AEDC does not use that designation and assigns those places to the nearest jurisdiction, so Cocos and Christmas Islands fall under Western Australia and Jervis Bay and Norfolk Island under New South Wales. It also identifies the child's residence, so it will not reconcile with a school-based count built on SCHOOLSTATE.
rationale: The dictionary defines the field and its one-digit integer format and points to the reference tables for the value list, and Table 2.1 of the published reference tables carries the eight StateID values against their state names.
evidence_quote: Code for state in which child resides.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'State identifier' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the code list is published in the reference tables the dictionary points to.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA) data and legislation
variable_description: The person key that ties a child's AEDC record to the rest of PLIDA, and the reason the collection is in this asset at all. Within AEDC it joins the five tables of a cycle, so a child's core record, domain scores, instrument background, language detail and special needs detail assemble on this column; across the asset it is the same key the Census, births, MBS, PBS, DOMINO and the tax products carry, so an AvEDI result can be read against a child's birth record, health history or family's payment history. ABS lists the AEDC among PLIDA's linked sources, naming the 2009, 2012, 2015 and 2018 collections on its data page while this asset carries six cycles, and the linkage is performed centrally against the person linkage spine rather than by matching names in this file.
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned for linkage with no meaning in its digits. It is not a student number, an enrolment identifier or an AEDC instrument identifier, so it can be matched but not decoded.
limitation: A child appears here only where their AvEDI record linked to the spine, and children who did not link are missing rather than untested, so AEDC coverage in PLIDA is lower than AEDC coverage in the national collection and the shortfall should not be assumed random. The key is also for the child, not the class or the family: TEACHERID and SCHOOLID group the record, and no parent or sibling identifier is carried, so a family cannot be assembled from this column alone.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA data page lists the Australian Early Development Census among the datasets brought into the asset and describes the central linkage of person records, which is what this column carries; the custodian description in the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic person identifier used across products.
evidence_quote: Australian Early Development Census, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018 - Measures how well children in their first year of full time school are developing across 5 important domains.
supersedes_rationale: The entry read 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 30 occurrences it never said that this is the column joining the five AEDC tables to each other and the AEDC to the rest of PLIDA, nor that linkage failure, not absence of assessment, explains a missing child.

value_domain: Teacher Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherATSI
variable_description: Whether the teacher who completed the instrument identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, asked directly as "Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent". It sits in the instrument background table with the CONSULTTYPE items about Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural consultants, and the point of the block is to describe who did the assessing rather than who was assessed. It is the column to use when testing whether teacher background is associated with reported outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, whose own status is on ATSI in the core table.
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 the teacher was not Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, 1 the teacher was, and 2 the teacher responded inconsistently to their own Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status.
limitation: It describes the teacher, not the child, so it cannot stand in for the child's Indigenous status anywhere. Code 2 is also a data quality state rather than a third identity: it marks contradictory answers within the teacher's own record, so quietly dropping it or folding it into 0 shifts the measured share of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander teachers in an unknown direction.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherATSI entry gives the origin definition, the instrument wording and all three labelled values, including the inconsistent-response code.
evidence_quote: Are you (the classroom teacher) of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Indigenous teacher' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and hid the third code for inconsistent responses.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TeacherID
variable_description: Which teacher filled in the instrument for this child, as a de-identified number. The dictionary describes it as a "unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information", and its analytic value is as the clustering unit: every AvEDI score is one teacher's judgement of one child, so children sharing a value here share a rater and their scores are not independent observations. SCHOOLID nests these teachers within schools, and CLASSTYPEA_1, CLASSTYPEB and CLASSTYPEC describe the class the teacher was reporting on.
value_definition: A right-justified integer, allocated for the collection and carrying no information about the teacher. The dictionary's variable page gives it a length of 11, while its appendix metadata shows the narrower format F6.0.
limitation: It is not a person key on the PLIDA spine, so a teacher cannot be joined to their own tax, payment or health records the way a child can through SYNTHETIC_AEUID; nothing about the teacher beyond TEACHERATSI is available. The dictionary also does not state that the code is stable between collections, so it should not be used to follow one teacher from 2009 to a later cycle.
rationale: The dictionary's TeacherID entry defines the code as unique and non-identifying and gives its integer format; the registry shows the field beside SCHOOLID and the class-type items that make it a clustering variable.
evidence_quote: The Teacher ID uses a unique numerical code to distinguish each teacher participating in the AEDC without providing any identifying information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Teacher identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never told a reader that this is the rater key their standard errors should account for, or that it does not reach the PLIDA spine.

value_domain: Time in class under one month, with completion intent (three values)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Tmsch
variable_description: Whether the child had been in class for less than one month when the instrument was started, and if so whether the teacher went on to fill it in anyway. The dictionary's reason for asking is that "If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC", and the teacher may then stop. This is why a row can exist with almost nothing on it: a value of 1 here is the explanation for empty domain scores and empty instrument items, and CANASSESS, asked only when this is a yes, records whether the teacher felt able to assess the child at all.
value_definition: A single-digit integer with three values: 0 no, 1 yes and skip the rest of the instrument, and 2 yes but the rest of the instrument will be completed.
limitation: The instrument asks about time in this class while the dictionary's description speaks of time at school, so a child who transferred in October after a full year elsewhere may be coded the same as a child who started school that month. It is also not a data quality flag on the responses that follow: a 1 means there are no responses to judge, while a 2 means the teacher went ahead on under a month's acquaintance and the scores stand in the file unmarked.
rationale: The dictionary's Tmsch entry gives the rationale, the instrument wording and all three values, including the distinction between skipping and completing the rest of the instrument, and records CanAssess as the follow-up item.
evidence_quote: If a child has attended less than one month of school their teacher may not have had sufficient time to accurately evaluate the child for the AEDC.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'In school for less than one month' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it read as a yes-or-no flag and never explained that one of its two yes values means the rest of the row was deliberately left blank.

value_domain: Count of missing domain scales (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry TotalMiss
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC scales could not be calculated for this child, defined by the dictionary as the "Total number of missing scales (0-5)". It is the sum of the five per-scale missing flags PHMiss, SCMiss, EMMiss, LCMiss and CGMiss, which the dictionary restricts to the master unit record file and which are not carried in the AEDC tables in this asset, so this count is the only summary of scale-level missingness available here. A scale goes missing when fewer than 75 per cent of that domain's instrument items were answered.
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5, one unit for each of physical health and wellbeing, social competence, emotional maturity, language and cognitive skills, and communication and general knowledge.
limitation: It does not say which scales are missing, so a value of 2 needs the five domain score columns checked one by one before an analysis can decide whether the loss matters. It is also not the complement of VALIDDOMAINS: a scale can be computed and still be ruled invalid because the child has special needs status or is three years old, so the two columns need not add to five.
rationale: The dictionary's TotalMiss entry gives the definition, the purpose and the 0 to 5 integer format, and the five per-scale flags immediately before it in the same section show what is being counted and that they are master-file-only fields.
evidence_quote: Total number of missing scales (0-5).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Total number of missing scales (0-5)' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and gave no hint that the per-scale flags behind the count are absent from this asset.

value_domain: Count of valid domain scores (0 to 5)
value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidDomains
variable_description: How many of the five AEDC domains yielded a usable score for this child, which the dictionary gives as being "To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid". It is the total of the five per-domain flags PHYSVALID, SOCVALID, EMOTVALID, LANGCOGVALID and COMGENVALID, and it is the input to the reporting rule: children with fewer than four valid domains are the ones VALIDINSTRUMENT marks as not counting. Use it as the first filter on any analysis of domain scores, ahead of the individual flags.
value_definition: A single-digit integer from 0 to 5. The dictionary publishes no value labels because the number is simply the count of domains for which the validity conditions were met.
limitation: A 0 does not mean an empty instrument. Children with special needs status have no valid domain scores by rule, so they sit at 0 while their teacher may have answered every question, and reading this column as a response-quality measure conflates an administrative exclusion with missing data. It also does not say which domains survived, so a study of one domain still has to read that domain's own validity flag.
rationale: The dictionary's ValidDomains entry gives the purpose and the one-digit integer format, and the domain validity entries beside it define the conditions being counted, including the special needs and age exclusions.
evidence_quote: To identify the number of domains in which the child is valid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Valid domains' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not give the range, did not say what makes a domain valid, and did not connect the column to the coverage rule it feeds.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry ValidInstrument
variable_description: Whether this child's completed instrument counts as valid for AEDC reporting, set from the number of domains that produced a score. The dictionary states the purpose as "To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule", the rule requiring that 80 per cent of the children in an area hold valid instruments before results for that area may be published. The AEDC Data Guidelines set out the arithmetic: divide the count of records with VALIDINSTRUMENT = 1 by the count with SPECIALNEEDS = 0. The dictionary records that the field was called ValidChecklist before the 2015 collection.
value_definition: A single-digit integer, 0 for no and 1 for yes, derived from VALIDDOMAINS with the threshold at four of the five domains.
limitation: A 0 is not a verdict on the teacher's answers. A child with special needs status has no valid domain scores by rule and therefore fails the four-domain test while holding a fully answered instrument, which is exactly why the coverage rule counts only children with SPECIALNEEDS = 0 in its denominator. The flag also governs whether an area may be reported, not whether an individual record may be used, so filtering child-level analysis on it discards children for a reason that belongs to their area's publication test.
rationale: The dictionary's ValidInstrument entry gives the purpose, the two-value code frame and the 2015 rename, and the AEDC Data Guidelines give the 80 per cent coverage rule and the exact numerator and denominator this flag is used in.
evidence_quote: To identify children with less than 4 valid domain scores for the purpose of calculating the 80 per cent Coverage Rule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Valid instrument indicator' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it named neither the four-domain threshold, nor the coverage rule the flag exists to serve, nor the earlier name of the field.

value_source: AEDC Data Dictionary v7.0 (Australian Government Department of Education, February 2025), entry Year
variable_description: The collection year of the AEDC cycle the row belongs to, defined by the dictionary as "The year in which the AvEDI was completed". Because the instrument is completed in the child's first year of full-time school, it is also, near enough, the year the child started school, which is what makes it the anchor for any before-and-after design built on an AEDC record. The AEDC products are split by cycle, so the column is near-constant within each table, and CYCLE carries the same collection numbered 1 to 6; the two differ only for Cycle 1, which the dictionary records as covering both 2009 and 2010.
value_definition: A four-digit integer. The collection years are 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2024, matching the six cycle tables in this asset, and the dictionary notes that Cycle 1 also takes in a 2010 follow-up collection, so a value of 2010 can occur in the first cycle.
limitation: It is not the date the instrument was filled in; MOC holds the month, which runs April to August, so events within a school year cannot be ordered against an AEDC record from this column alone. Nor is it a birth cohort: children in one collection year run across the AEDC age categories from under five years to over six years, and AGEINMONTHS or AGECAT is needed before an age comparison means anything.
rationale: The dictionary's Year entry gives the definition and the four-digit integer format, the Cycle entry beside it confirms the six numbered collections, and the MOC entry gives the April to August completion window that this column does not carry.
evidence_quote: The year in which the AvEDI was completed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Year that the information relates to' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 30 occurrences it never said that only six values occur or that the column is fixed within each cycle table.
